programme_name: pDC Maturation and Type I IFN Priming
functional_description: This signature defines committed plasmacytoid dendritic cells with established identity and enhanced capacity for Type I interferon production. The program integrates master pDC transcription factors (TCF4, IRF7, IRF8) with pDC-selective surface markers (LILRA4) and components of the secretory pathway required for robust cytokine and antibody production.
key_evidence: LILRA4: pDC-restricted surface receptor essential for functional pDC identity and immune modulation
TCF4: Master transcription factor (E2-2) required for pDC lineage specification and maintenance
IRF7: Central Type I IFN production transcription factor and pDC signature regulator
IRF8: Core pDC transcription factor controlling lineage commitment and activation responses
PLD4: pDC-enriched nuclease implicated in nucleic acid sensing and TLR9 signaling
JCHAIN: Immunoglobulin joining chain indicating plasma cell-like secretory differentiation capacity
SSR4: Translocon-associated protein enabling robust ER protein translocation for cytokine secretion
MZB1: Marks cells with high proliferative potential and secretory capacity in B cell lineage
ITM2C: ER/Golgi resident protein involved in protein trafficking in secretory-active cells
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining: LILRA4+TCF4+IRF7+ cells with intracellular IRF8 and phospho-IRF7; functional validation by pI:C or CpG stimulation measuring IFN-α/β secretion; compare against cDC1 (XCR1+TAP1+) and cDC2 (CD1c+FCER1A+) controls

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated HLA class II molecule expression and assembly machinery, dominated by HLA-DR, HLA-DP, and HLA-DQ heterodimer components alongside CD74 chaperone. While cDC1 comprise only 42.5% of activating cells, the strong ANOVA signal (F-stat=4472.4) suggests selective upregulation in this subset, consistent with cDC1's role in bridging innate and adaptive immunity through antigen presentation.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA: HLA class II alpha chain core component, essential for MHC-II presentation
CD74: Critical chaperone for MHC class II assembly and peptide loading
HLA-DPA1/HLA-DPB1: HLA-DP heterodimer components, MHC class II presentation
HLA-DRB1: HLA-DR heterodimer beta chain, dominant MHC-II isotype
HLA-DMA/HLA-DMB: Peptide exchange catalysts for MHC class II loading
HLA-DQA1/HLA-DQB1: HLA-DQ heterodimer components, MHC class II presentation
CST3: Cysteine protease inhibitor, supports antigen processing endosomal pH control
suggested_validation: Validate cDC1-specificity by flow cytometry sorting (CLEC9+XCR1+BATF3+) followed by bulk RNA-seq to confirm preferential HLA-II expression versus cDC2. Cross-reference with single-cell transcriptomics to establish if this signature marks activated cDC1 subset. Note: Lack of canonical cDC1 markers (BATF3, IRF8, XCR1, CLEC9A) and cross-presentation genes (TAP1/2, NLRC5) suggests this is a secondary consequence of cDC1 activation rather than a core identity programme.

programme_name: pDC maturation and plasma cell differentiation
functional_description: This signature represents activated pDCs undergoing terminal differentiation toward plasmablast/plasma cell fate, characterized by co-expression of master pDC transcription factors (TCF4, IRF7) with plasma cell differentiation markers (JCHAIN, MZB1). The constellation reflects pDCs that have integrated nucleic acid signals and are transitioning from antigen presentation toward antibody secretion.
key_evidence: TCF4: Master pDC lineage-determining transcription factor; essential for pDC development
IRF7: Type I IFN master regulator; hallmark of activated pDCs; synergizes with TCF4
CLEC4C: pDC-specific C-type lectin receptor; nucleic acid sensing co-receptor
LILRA4: pDC-restricted inhibitory receptor; negatively regulates TLR responses; pDC identity marker
JCHAIN: Plasma cell/plasmablast differentiation marker; enables polymeric immunoglobulin assembly
MZB1: Marginal zone B cell and plasma cell-associated protein; marks differentiation toward antibody-secreting phenotype
GZMB: Cytotoxic effector; pDCs express GZMB upon activation; indicates functional maturation
PTPRS: pDC migration and trafficking regulator; involved in homing and tissue localization
DERL3: ER-resident protein quality control; increased in plasma cells with high secretory demand
suggested_validation: Co-stain activated pDCs (SIGLEC-H+ BST2+ TCF4+ IRF7+) for plasma cell markers (CD38, CD27, JCHAIN protein); perform flow cytometry sort and RT-qPCR validation of JCHAIN/MZB1 co-expression; assess IgA/IgG secretion capacity and Type I IFN production in JCHAIN+ versus JCHAIN- pDC subsets

functional_description: This signature reflects active cell cycle progression with predominant S/G2-M phase enrichment in cycling DC progenitors. The gene set combines mitotic spindle organization machinery (NUSAP1, TUBA1B, TUBB), cell cycle checkpoint regulation (CKS1B), and chromatin remodeling (HMGN2, HMGB1, HMGB2, H2AFZ, H3F3A) required for chromosome condensation and segregation during mitosis.
key_evidence: STMN1: Canonical S/G2-M cell cycle marker, microtubule dynamics regulation
CKS1B: CDK-binding protein essential for cell cycle progression through G1/S and G2/M checkpoints
NUSAP1: Spindle microtubule organization during mitosis
TUBA1B, TUBB: Microtubule cytoskeleton assembly for mitotic spindle formation
HMGN2, HMGB1, HMGB2: Chromatin-associated proteins facilitating chromosome condensation during mitosis
H2AFZ, H3F3A: Histone variants incorporated during active transcription and DNA replication
Pre-pDC Cycling 32%: Direct confirmation of cycling progenitor enrichment in activating population
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry with Ki-67/PCNA co-staining on Pre-cDC and Pre-pDC Cycling populations; confirm cell cycle phase distribution via Hoechst/DNA content analysis; validate mitotic protein expression (phospho-histone H3, Aurora kinase B activity) in sorted activated cells.

functional_description: This signature represents a cDC1-enriched transcriptional programme centred on MHC class II antigen presentation machinery. The dominant expression of HLA-DR, HLA-DP, and HLA-DQ heterodimers alongside CD74 (CLIP-containing invariant chain) and HLA-DM editing components indicates functional capacity for exogenous antigen presentation via endosomal-lysosomal pathways. The presence of CLEC9A confirms cDC1 identity while accessory proteases (CPVL, PSAP) support antigen processing.
key_evidence: CD74: MHC-II chaperone and antigen presentation licensing factor, essential for CLIP-mediated peptide loading
HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1: MHC-II DR heterodimer α and β chains, primary presenters in humans
HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1: MHC-II DP heterodimer components with specialized antigen-uptake roles
HLA-DQA1, HLA-DQB1: MHC-II DQ heterodimer α and β chains for diverse peptide presentation
HLA-DMA, HLA-DMB: MHC-II editing molecules that catalyse CLIP removal and peptide exchange
CLEC9A: cDC1-specific C-type lectin receptor confirming cell-type identity
CPVL: Carboxypeptidase for peptide trimming in endosomal processing
PSAP: Saposin precursor supporting lysosomal antigen processing capacity
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of CD74, HLA-DR, and CLEC9A on cDC1 subsets; cross-presentation assay using model peptides to confirm functional MHC-II presentation; RNA-seq validation comparing cDC1 vs cDC2 MHC-II gene expression ratios

functional_description: This signature reflects pDC commitment toward antibody-secreting plasma cell differentiation, characterized by upregulation of immunoglobulin J chain and plasma cell-associated transcriptional regulators. The enrichment of genes involved in protein secretion, ER-Golgi trafficking, and cell proliferation control suggests active terminal differentiation of pDC toward antibody-producing effector cells rather than Type I IFN production.
key_evidence: JCHAIN: Immunoglobulin J chain is a canonical marker of plasma cells and B cell terminal differentiation, rarely expressed in typical pDC
MZB1: Marginal zone B cell protein involved in cell proliferation and plasma cell development
PTPRS: pDC-associated phosphatase involved in pDC maturation and migration control
PPP1R14B: Innate immune response regulator consistent with pDC activation state
DERL3: ER-resident protein required for protein folding/degradation quality control in antibody-secreting cells
BCL11A: Transcriptional regulator of B cell and plasma cell differentiation
UGCG: Glycosphingolipid synthesis involved in membrane trafficking during secretory activation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry and qPCR validation of JCHAIN, MZB1, and BCL11A expression in sorted pDC subsets; immunofluorescence to distinguish plasma cell-differentiating pDC from canonical IFN-producing pDC using JCHAIN vs. IRF7 staining

functional_description: This signature reflects active cell cycle progression in proliferating DC progenitors, dominated by Pre-pDC Cycling cells (58.5%). The enrichment of microtubule/tubulin proteins (TUBB, TUBA1B), mitotic regulators (CKS1B), and chromatin remodeling factors (HMGB1/2, HMGN1/2, H3F3A) indicates S/G2-M phase transit. Co-expression in Pre-cDC (38.5%) suggests heightened proliferative capacity across bipotent progenitor compartments.
key_evidence: STMN1: Canonical S/G2-M phase regulator; microtubule dynamics essential for mitosis
CKS1B: CDK-binding protein required for G1/S and G2/M checkpoint progression
TUBB, TUBA1B: Mitotic spindle assembly and cytokinesis machinery
HMGB1, HMGB2: Chromatin condensation and segregation during mitosis
HMGN1, HMGN2: Dynamic chromatin remodeling associated with active transcription in dividing cells
H3F3A: Replication-dependent histone variant incorporation during S phase
PTMA, ANP32B: Anti-apoptotic factors protecting cycling cells from death
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry with PCNA/Ki67 co-staining and BrdU incorporation assays to confirm S/G2-M enrichment; FACS-sorted Pre-pDC Cycling vs Pre-pDC quiescent comparison; RNA velocity analysis to map progenitor progression through cell cycle phases.

programme_name: Pre-cDC protein synthesis and metabolic activity
functional_description: This signature reflects active protein synthesis and basal metabolic processes in committed cDC progenitors. The predominance of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS17, RPL37A, RPS23), translation factors (EEF1B2), and glycolytic enzymes (GAPDH, TPI1) indicates high translational capacity typical of proliferating progenitors. HLA-DRA and LYZ suggest early antigen-presenting capacity emerging in Pre-cDC.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS17, RPL37A, RPS23: Ribosomal structural proteins indicating active protein synthesis machinery
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor supporting sustained protein translation
GAPDH, TPI1: Glycolytic enzymes reflecting elevated metabolic demand of progenitor cells
HLA-DRA: MHC class II alpha chain expressing Pre-cDC identity
LYZ: Lysozyme expression indicating antibacterial capacity emerging in committed cDC
TMSB4X: Actin regulator supporting cell migration and differentiation during commitment
GSTP1, MT-CO3: Detoxification and respiratory chain components supporting metabolic homeostasis
suggested_validation: Validate Pre-cDC identity through co-expression analysis with CLEC12A, PTPRS, and CCR7; confirm absence of pDC markers (SIGLEC-H, SPIB, IRF8) to exclude cDC1 differentiation; assess cell cycle status to distinguish quiescent from cycling Pre-cDC populations using MKI67/PCNA co-staining.

functional_description: This signature reflects pDC progenitor specification and early proliferation, driven by TCF4 and SPIB-mediated transcriptional programming characteristic of the pDC lineage. The co-expression of cell cycle regulators (STMN1) and IRF7/IRF8 with pDC-enriched transcription factors indicates Pre-pDC progenitors transitioning through active proliferation phases toward pDC maturation.
key_evidence: TCF4: Master transcription factor for pDC specification; highest ranked gene in signature
SPIB: Lymphoid-specific PU-box activator; defining pDC lineage commitment marker
IRF7: Interferon regulatory factor essential for pDC function and type I IFN responses
IRF8: cDC1/pDC lineage bifurcation factor; present in pDC progenitors
STMN1: Microtubule destabilizer; S/G2-M phase cell cycle marker consistent with 22% Pre-pDC Cycling
CLEC4C: pDC-restricted C-type lectin receptor; mature pDC marker emerging in progenitors
CCDC50: Chromatin-associated protein potentially supporting active transcription in cycling progenitors
HMGN2: Chromatin remodeling protein; marks transcriptionally active differentiation state
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry sorting for TCF4+SPIB+IRF7+ progenitors with STMN1 expression analysis; ATAC-seq to confirm PU-box chromatin accessibility; qPCR validation of IRF7/IRF8 ratio to establish lineage bias trajectory from ASDC through Pre-pDC Cycling to mature pDC

programme_name: pDC cytotoxic and plasma cell differentiation
functional_description: This signature represents activated pDCs with cytotoxic effector function and antibody-secreting differentiation capacity, characterized by granzyme B expression and J-chain-mediated immunoglobulin production. The combination of pDC-restricted markers (LILRA4, TCF4, IRF7) with cytolytic machinery suggests terminal pDC maturation toward hybrid pDC-plasma cell phenotypes capable of both Type I IFN and antibody production.
key_evidence: LILRA4: pDC-specific inhibitory receptor, diagnostic pDC marker with 91% composition
TCF4: Master pDC transcription factor (E2-2), essential for pDC lineage specification
IRF7: Critical pDC transcription factor for Type I IFN and antiviral responses
GZMB: Cytotoxic effector protein, atypical for pDCs but consistent with activated/differentiated state
JCHAIN: Plasma cell-associated immunoglobulin joining chain, indicates antibody production capacity
PLD4: pDC-enriched nucleic acid sensor involved in TLR-mediated responses
TSPAN13: pDC-specific tetraspanin implicated in TLR signaling
IRF7: Mediates Type I IFN production downstream of TLR7/TLR9 sensing
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of pDCs (LILRA4+/CLEC4C+/BST2+) with GZMB and intracellular immunoglobulin; assess IRF7 phosphorylation status and Type I IFN secretion in GZMB+ subset; single-cell TCR/BCR capture to confirm plasma cell differentiation trajectory

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein and translation machinery expression in DC progenitors, particularly cycling Pre-pDC and Pre-cDC populations undergoing active protein synthesis during proliferation. The dominance of ribosomal proteins (RPS23, RPS24, RPS17, RPS2, RPL4, RPLP0) and translation factors (EEF1B2) indicates heightened translational demand, consistent with the metabolic requirements of proliferating progenitor cells.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPS24, RPS17, RPS2, RPL4, RPLP0: Core ribosomal proteins; elevated in rapidly dividing Pre-pDC Cycling (29%) and Pre-pDC (23.5%) populations
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor; supports active protein synthesis during progenitor expansion
DUT: Nucleotide metabolism enzyme; dUTP hydrolysis supports DNA synthesis in cycling cells (compatible with 29% Pre-pDC Cycling)
H3F3A, H2AFY: Histone variants; chromatin remodeling during cell cycle progression
PPIA: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase; protein folding chaperone supporting synthesis of new proteins
GPX1: Antioxidant enzyme; protects against ROS during high metabolic activity in proliferating progenitors
suggested_validation: Correlate signature with Ki-67/MKI67 and PCNA expression; validate in Pre-pDC Cycling and Pre-cDC populations using ribosomal profiling or polysome analysis; assess protein synthesis rates via SUnSET or puromycin incorporation assays in sorted DC progenitors.

functional_description: This signature represents a dominant MHC class II antigen presentation programme enriched in cDC1 cells (57.5%), featuring complete HLA-DR, HLA-DP, and HLA-DQ heterodimer components alongside the critical chaperone CD74. The programme supports professional antigen presentation capacity with co-expression of processing enzymes (HLA-DMA, CPVL) and cytoskeletal regulators, indicating active antigen-loading and presentation machinery.
key_evidence: CD74: Essential MHC class II chaperone for peptide loading and antigen presentation
HLA-DRA/DRB1: Complete HLA-DR heterodimer, primary MHC class II presentation molecule
HLA-DPA1/DPB1: Complete HLA-DP heterodimer, specialised in presentation pathway
HLA-DQA1/DQB1: Complete HLA-DQ heterodimer, tertiary MHC class II complex
HLA-DMA: Peptide exchange factor facilitating MHC class II peptide loading
CPVL: Carboxypeptidase supporting antigen processing in presentation pathway
TMSB4X: Actin regulation supporting dendritic cell migration and antigen capture
suggested_validation: Validate through flow cytometry co-expression analysis of HLA-DR/DP/DQ with CD74 on sorted cDC1 (CLEC9A+XCR1+); confirm MHC class II presentation capacity via peptide-MHC tetramer binding assays; compare with cDC2 (higher overall MHC-II) and pDC (lower MHC-II expression) to establish cDC1-specific regulation patterns.

functional_description: This signature reflects robust MHC class II antigen presentation machinery in cDC1, despite cDC1's canonical role in MHC-I cross-presentation. The enrichment of HLA-II genes (HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1, HLA-DQA1, HLA-DQB1) alongside CD74 (invariant chain) and HLA-DMA indicates coordinated expression of multiple HLA-II isotypes with their chaperones. This reflects cDC1's capacity for constitutive MHC-II presentation of exogenous antigens in parallel with their primary cross-presentation function.
key_evidence: CD74: MHC-II chaperone and invariant chain, essential for MHC-II loading and trafficking
HLA-DRA/HLA-DRB1: Classical DR isotype proteins for MHC-II presentation
HLA-DPA1/HLA-DPB1: DP isotype for MHC-II presentation, typically cDC-enriched
HLA-DQA1/HLA-DQB1: DQ isotype for MHC-II presentation
HLA-DMA: Non-classical MHC-II molecule regulating peptide loading in endosomal compartments
CPVL: Carboxypeptidase for MHC-II peptide trimming in antigen processing
FCGRT: FcRn mediates antibody transport and endosomal recycling pathways relevant to antigen capture
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of MHC-II surface expression (HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ) on CLEC9A+ XCR1+ cDC1 versus cDC2; functional assays measuring MHC-II-restricted CD4 T cell activation capacity; comparison with published cDC1 versus cDC2 transcriptomic datasets to confirm cDC1-skewed activation

programme_name: MHC Class II Antigen Presentation Program
functional_description: This signature reflects elevated MHC class II antigen presentation capacity, dominated by HLA-DR, HLA-DP, and HLA-DQ heterodimer components alongside CD74 and HLA-DM chaperones essential for peptide loading. The programme is enriched in cDC1 (59.5%) despite being class II-focused, suggesting cDC1 maintain robust MHC-II presentation capacity for CD4+ T cell activation alongside their primary cross-presentation function.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1: Core HLA-DR alpha/beta chains for class II presentation
HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1: HLA-DP heterodimer components
HLA-DQA1, HLA-DQB1: HLA-DQ heterodimer components
CD74: Essential MHC-II chaperone and peptide exchange facilitator
HLA-DMA, HLA-DMB: HLA-DM editing complex for peptide optimization
CPVL: Endosomal carboxypeptidase involved in peptide trimming
CST3: Cysteine protease inhibitor regulating proteolytic processing
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of surface HLA-DR/DP/DQ expression and functional assay of MHC-II-restricted antigen presentation capacity in sorted cDC1. Cross-reference with cDC2 signatures to confirm relative enrichment and assess whether cDC1 upregulation of class II machinery correlates with specific inflammatory contexts or maturation states.

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened MHC class II-mediated antigen presentation machinery, marked by coordinated upregulation of HLA-DR, HLA-DP, and HLA-DQ heterodimers alongside the essential chaperone CD74 and peptide-loading factor HLA-DMA. The enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPL, RPS genes) indicates active protein synthesis supporting robust antigen processing and presentation, characteristic of both cDC1 and cDC2 populations with antigen-presenting capacity.
key_evidence: CD74: MHC class II chaperone essential for peptide loading and trafficking
HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1: MHC class II molecules required for CD4+ T cell activation
HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1: MHC class II heterodimer components for antigen presentation
HLA-DQB1: MHC class II molecule supporting diverse antigen presentation
HLA-DMA: MHC class II peptide-loading factor enabling productive antigen presentation
RPL4, RPL7A, RPS2, RPS17, RPS23, RPS24: Ribosomal proteins supporting protein synthesis
TMSB4X: Cytoskeletal regulator supporting DC migration and maturation
suggested_validation: This signature is enriched in both cDC1 (41%) and cDC2 (37%) but lacks cDC1-specific markers (BATF3, IRF8, CLEC9A, XCR1) and cross-presentation components (TAP1, TAP2, NLRC5). Validate by: (1) sorting cDC1 vs cDC2 and quantifying HLA-DR/DP/DQ expression ratios; (2) comparing with cross-presentation-specific genes (TAP1, TAP2); (3) assessing whether this reflects MHC-II presentation capacity rather than cDC1 identity per se.

functional_description: This signature reflects committed Pre-cDC progenitors with elevated MHC class II antigen presentation machinery (HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DM, CD74) combined with constitutive ribosomal and translational activity. The dominance of Pre-cDC cells (54%) and cDC1 (35%) indicates a differentiation programme supporting imminent cDC lineage commitment with functional capacity for professional antigen presentation.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA: core MHC-II alpha chain; hallmark of Pre-cDC maturation and antigen presentation competence
CD74: MHC-II chaperone essential for peptide loading and Ii chain regulation; Pre-cDC-specific expression
HLA-DRB1: MHC-II beta chain; Pre-cDC express all three HLA-DR, -DP, -DQ pathways
HLA-DPA1 and HLA-DPB1: complete HLA-DP heterodimer expression; Pre-cDC-enriched
HLA-DMA: MHC-II peptide exchange catalyst; marks functionally mature Pre-cDC
RPS24, RPS23, RPL4, RPS17, EEF1B2: elevated translation machinery consistent with anabolic Pre-cDC state
CST3 and GSTP1: oxidative stress and protease regulation supporting antigen processing
MT-CO3: mitochondrial respiration supporting energetic demands of Pre-cDC
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry confirming HLA-DR++, CD74+, CLEC12A+ Pre-cDC phenotype; validate cDC1 bias via IRF8 expression; assess MHC-II peptide loading capacity via DM-dependent assays; confirm absence of pDC markers (SIGLEC-H, SPIB)

functional_description: This signature represents a robust MHC class II antigen presentation programme enriched in cDC1 cells (54.5% of top activators). The programme encompasses complete HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, and HLA-DP heterodimer components plus CD74 (invariant chain chaperone) and HLA-DM, indicating coordinated assembly and peptide loading of MHC class II molecules for CD4+ T cell activation.
key_evidence: CD74: MHC class II invariant chain; essential chaperone for HLA assembly and trafficking
HLA-DRA/HLA-DRB1: Complete HLA-DR heterodimer components; major MHC class II presentation pathway
HLA-DPA1/HLA-DPB1: HLA-DP heterodimer; distinct MHC class II pathway
HLA-DQA1/HLA-DQB1: HLA-DQ heterodimer; alternative MHC class II presentation
HLA-DMA: Peptide exchange factor in endosomal compartments; critical for MHC class II loading
CPVL: Carboxypeptidase in endosomal-lysosomal pathway; processes peptides for MHC II presentation
CLEC9A: cDC1-specific marker confirms cellular context of signature
TMSB4X: Cytoskeletal protein supporting dendritic cell migration and antigen trafficking
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry quantifying surface HLA-DR/DP/DQ expression and CD74 protein levels on cDC1 vs cDC2/pDC; functional assay measuring peptide-MHC class II loading capacity; comparison with cDC2-specific MHC II signatures to validate cDC1 enrichment despite mixed composition

functional_description: This signature reflects enhanced MHC class II antigen presentation machinery, predominantly active in cDC1 (58%) alongside cDC2. The coordinated upregulation of HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ heterodimers with CD74 chaperone indicates robust antigen processing and presentation capacity. This represents a cross-presentation-competent cDC1 state with secondary MHC-II function rather than exclusive cDC1 cross-presentation identity.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1: Core MHC-II α/β chains defining antigen presentation complex
HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1: MHC-II DP heterodimer components, elevated in presenting DC
HLA-DQA1, HLA-DQB1: MHC-II DQ heterodimer components, broad DC expression
CD74: Essential chaperone for MHC-II assembly and peptide loading in endosomal compartments
HLA-DMA, HLA-DMB: Catalytic chaperones facilitating peptide exchange in MHC-II pathway
CPVL: Carboxypeptidase involved in peptide trimming during antigen processing
cDC1 enrichment (58%): Confirms signature activation in cross-presenting DC subset
suggested_validation: Compare with cDC1-restricted cross-presentation markers (TAP1, TAP2, TAPBP, NLRC5, XCR1, CLEC9A); validate MHC-II transcriptional drivers (CIITA, RFX5); confirm functional MHC-II presentation capacity via peptide-MHC-II binding assays or MHC-II-restricted T cell stimulation.

functional_description: This signature reflects the core transcriptional and developmental identity of plasmacytoid dendritic cells, centred on master regulators TCF4 (E2-2), IRF7, and SPIB that establish pDC lineage specification and functional competence. The presence of IL3RA (CD123), pDC-specific markers, and IRF8 alongside lineage-determining factors indicates active maintenance of pDC identity in both mature and pre-pDC developmental stages.
key_evidence: TCF4: Master pDC transcription factor (E2-2), essential for pDC lineage specification and development
IRF7: Central Type I IFN transcription factor and pDC effector function coordinator
SPIB: Lymphoid-specific PU-box transcription factor critical for pDC differentiation
IL3RA: pDC-defining surface marker (CD123), functionally linked to pDC survival
IRF8: Collaborative transcription factor for pDC commitment and cDC distinction
JCHAIN: Immunoglobulin binding protein suggesting plasma cell-like secretory capacity associated with pDC cytokine production
CCDC50: pDC-enriched gene of unknown function, consistently marks pDC transcriptional programmes
PLD4: Single-strand DNA nuclease implicated in TLR9-mediated pDC responses
ITM2C: pDC-enriched trafficking/vesicular protein supporting intracellular nucleic acid sensing
MZB1: Pre-plasma cell/activated B cell marker, reflects pDC capacity for high-rate cytokine secretion
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry sorting for SIGLEC-H+BST2+LILRA4+ cells followed by RT-qPCR validation of TCF4, IRF7, SPIB co-expression; in situ hybridisation to confirm pDC spatial distribution and developmental stage-specific expression in bone marrow niches

functional_description: This signature reflects core MHC class II antigen presentation capacity, dominated by HLA-DR, HLA-DP, and HLA-DQ heterodimer components alongside the CD74 chaperone essential for peptide loading. The predominance of cDC2 (48.5%) in activating cells confirms this represents a fundamental cDC2 function, with supporting Pre-cDC and cDC1 co-expression indicating shared antigen presentation competence across classical DC lineages.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA: α-chain of HLA-DR heterodimer, canonical MHC-II molecule in cDC2
HLA-DRB1: β-chain of HLA-DR, most abundant MHC-II presentation complex in professional APCs
HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1: HLA-DP heterodimer components, secondary MHC-II pathway in cDC2
HLA-DQA1, HLA-DQB1: HLA-DQ heterodimer components, tertiary MHC-II presentation route
CD74: Invariant chain and MHC-II chaperone for peptide loading and intracellular trafficking
HLA-DMA, HLA-DMB: Non-classical MHC-II molecules regulating peptide exchange in endosomal compartments
FCGRT: IgG Fc receptor supporting antibody-mediated antigen presentation enhancement
FTH1, CST3: Iron homeostasis and protease inhibition supporting sustained antigen processing
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of surface HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ expression on sorted cDC2 (CLEC12A+ CD1c+ CD14-low); functional assay of peptide presentation capacity using MHC-II-restricted T cell proliferation with cDC2 vs cDC1; assess whether cDC2 show higher absolute MHC-II expression than cDC1 in this cohort

programme_name: MHC-II antigen presentation and protein synthesis
functional_description: This signature reflects a constitutive antigen presentation programme dominated by HLA class II molecules (HLA-DRA, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1, HLA-DMA, HLA-DQB1) and the chaperone CD74, coupled with active protein synthesis machinery. The signature is characteristic of professional antigen-presenting cells with high MHC-II expression, though the enrichment in cDC1 (50%) suggests this represents a subset of cDC1 with particularly active HLA-II-mediated exogenous antigen presentation capacity.
key_evidence: CD74: essential chaperone for HLA class II assembly and peptide loading; core antigen presentation function
HLA-DRA, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1, HLA-DMA, HLA-DQB1: complete HLA class II presentation pathway genes; expected in all DC subsets but elevated in cDC1 subset
TMSB4X: actin-binding protein supporting cell motility and antigen acquisition; relevant to DC migration
RPL4, RPS23, RPS24, RPS26, RPS17, EEF1B2: ribosomal and translation machinery; indicates active protein synthesis for MHC-II and co-stimulatory molecules
ACTG1: cytoskeletal protein supporting DC morphology and antigen sampling
NDUFV2: mitochondrial complex I component; energy supply for active antigen presentation
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry measuring surface HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ expression across cDC1/cDC2/pDC subsets; compare with cDC1-specific markers (CLEC9A, XCR1) to confirm this represents a specialized cDC1 subpopulation. Assess functional capacity using MHC-II-restricted T cell activation assays with exogenous antigen.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated protein synthesis machinery and metabolic activity in pre-committed DC progenitors, particularly Pre-cDC and early cDC1 cells. The dominance of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPL4, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPL7A) and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) indicates high translational demand consistent with active differentiation and proliferation. Co-expression of myeloid activation markers (AIF1, CD74, GSTP1) and oxidative phosphorylation genes (MT-CO2, COX5A) suggests metabolically active progenitors engaged in lineage commitment.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPL4, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPL7A: Coordinated ribosomal subunit upregulation indicating active protein synthesis during progenitor differentiation
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor supporting sustained protein production in dividing/differentiating cells
AIF1: Calcium-binding myeloid activation marker enriched in monocytic and DC lineages
CD74: MHC-II chaperone essential for antigen presentation capacity in developing cDCs
TMSB4X: Actin-regulating protein promoting cell migration and proliferation in myeloid progenitors
GSTP1, MT-CO2, COX5A: Detoxification and oxidative phosphorylation supporting metabolic demands of differentiating progenitors
Cell composition: 35% cDC1 + 33.5% Pre-cDC = 68.5% committed to cDC lineage, indicating cDC progenitor-skewed signature
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry co-staining of CD74 with Pre-cDC markers (CLEC12A, PTPRS) and S-phase markers (Ki67, PCNA) to confirm metabolically active, committed cDC progenitors. Assess translational capacity via puromycin incorporation assays in sorted Pre-cDC versus mature cDC populations.

programme_name: MHC-II Antigen Presentation and cDC2 Maturation
functional_description: This signature reflects a cDC2-dominant programme centred on MHC class II antigen presentation machinery, with co-expression of maturation markers and iron homeostasis genes. The coordinated upregulation of HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, and HLA-DP heterodimeric components, along with the peptide-loading chaperone CD74 and HLA-DM, indicates active antigen processing and presentation capacity characteristic of differentiated cDC2.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA: Core MHC-II α-chain; essential cDC2 antigen presentation
HLA-DRB1: MHC-II β-chain; primary cDC2 presentation molecule
HLA-DQB1 + HLA-DQA1: MHC-II DQ heterodimer; cDC2-enriched presentation pathway
HLA-DPB1 + HLA-DPA1: MHC-II DP heterodimer; alternative cDC2 presentation route

programme_name: Pre-cDC metabolic priming and stress resilience
functional_description: This signature reflects a metabolic and nucleotide-binding protein programme enriched in Pre-cDC progenitors, characterized by glycolytic enzyme upregulation (GAPDH, ENO1, TPI1, PKM), ribosomal proteins (RPS2, RPS24), and stress-response factors. The signature supports active protein synthesis, metabolic flux, and oxidative stress buffering required for committed cDC differentiation with minimal cell cycle genes, suggesting metabolic priming rather than proliferation-driven commitment.

GAPDH, ENO1, TPI1, PKM: glycolytic enzyme cluster indicating elevated glucose metabolism characteristic of differentiating Pre-cDC

functional_description: This signature represents a constitutive transcriptional programme enriched in Pre-cDC cells (59.5% of top activators), characterised by fundamental cellular housekeeping functions including ribosomal proteins, RNA-binding proteins, and cytoskeletal regulators. The signature reflects baseline metabolic and translational activity rather than lineage-specific differentiation or proliferation signals, consistent with steady-state progenitor cell physiology.

RPS24, RPS23, RPS17: Ribosomal structural proteins indicating active translation machinery required for baseline protein synthesis in metabolically active progenitors

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated protein synthesis capacity and actin cytoskeletal dynamics in committed cDC progenitors. The enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPL37A), translation factors (PPIA), and actin-binding proteins (TMSB4X, COTL1) indicates active translational machinery supporting cDC1 differentiation. The co-expression of CD74 and HLA-DRA suggests early MHC-II antigen presentation competence in maturing cDC.

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened cellular metabolism and protein synthesis activity in committed pre-cDC progenitors, characterized by elevated ribosomal proteins, mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation components, and actin-cytoskeletal regulators. The dominance of Pre-cDC cells (57.5%) with secondary cDC1 representation (25.5%) indicates metabolic priming associated with cDC lineage commitment and maturation. The enrichment of housekeeping/metabolic genes rather than lineage-defining markers suggests this represents an intermediate developmental state requiring sustained biosynthetic capacity.

TMSB4X: Actin sequestration protein regulating cytoskeletal dynamics required for cell migration and progenitor differentiation
CD74: MHC class II chaperone indicating immunological competence and antigen presentation priming in committed pre-cDC

YBX1, PPIA: RNA-binding and protein-folding chaperones managing protein homeostasis during intensive biosynthesis

Validate with Seahorse mitochondrial stress test comparing Pre-cDC oxidative capacity to mature and cycling progenitors. RNA-velocity analysis to confirm pre-cDC→cDC1 differentiation trajectory enrichment.

functional_description: This signature reflects a metabolically active Pre-cDC population with enhanced glycolytic capacity, oxidative phosphorylation, and innate antimicrobial defence mechanisms. The co-expression of lysozyme, ribonuclease, and cystatin alongside metabolic enzymes indicates progenitors preparing for microbial antigen processing and presentation.

PTMA, HMGN2: chromatin remodelling factors supporting active transcription in metabolically engaged progenitors

programme_name: pDC Type I Interferon Maturation Programme
functional_description: This signature represents activated plasmacytoid dendritic cells (88.5% pDC) characterized by Type I interferon production machinery and pDC-specific identity markers. The programme combines master pDC transcription factors (IRF7, TCF4) with immunoglobulin production capacity (JCHAIN, MZB1) and cytotoxic effector functions (GZMB), indicating fully differentiated, activated pDCs capable of both innate antiviral responses and adaptive immune coordination.

IL3RA: CD123 surface marker; critical for pDC development and CSF2RA-independent cytokine signalling
TCF4: E2-2 transcription factor; essential master regulator of pDC lineage specification
JCHAIN: Immunoglobulin joining chain; indicates pDC capacity for antibody production and B-cell help
MZB1: Positive regulator of B-cell proliferation; consistent with pDC-B cell interaction
GZMB: Granzyme B; indicates pDC cytotoxic capability against infected/malignant cells
PLD4: Nucleic acid sensing-associated nuclease; supports TLR7/9 signalling pathway activation

functional_description: This signature reflects constitutive metabolic activity and nuclear protein organization in committed cDC progenitors. The enrichment of glycolytic enzymes (LDHA), nucleosome-associated proteins (HMGN2, HMGB1), RNA-binding proteins (HNRNPA1, HNRNPA2B1), and cytoskeletal regulators (TMSB4X) indicates active transcriptional remodeling and metabolic support for differentiation. The absence of cell cycle markers and lineage-determining TFs suggests this is a quiescent-to-intermediate Pre-cDC state preparing for terminal maturation.
key_evidence: LDHA: Anaerobic glycolysis upregulation supporting Pre-cDC metabolic demands
HMGN2, HMGB1: Nucleoprotein scaffolding for open chromatin in differentiating progenitors
HNRNPA1, HNRNPA2B1: RNA processing during Pre-cDC transcriptional reprogramming
TMSB4X: Actin dynamics required for Pre-cDC morphological changes and migration
ANXA2: Calcium-dependent signaling in progenitor maturation pathways
YBX1: DNA/RNA binding protein supporting transcriptional regulation during commitment
78.5% Pre-cDC composition: Exclusive enrichment in committed cDC lineage
suggested_validation: Sort Pre-cDC (CLEC12A+ PTPRS+) and validate LDHA/ANXA2 protein expression and glycolytic flux by flow cytometry and Seahorse analysis; compare to ASDC and mature cDC1/cDC2 to confirm metabolic state differences.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein and translation machinery expression across early DC progenitors, particularly Pre-pDC and cDC2 precursors. The enrichment of 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit components (RPS2, RPS17, RPS23, RPS24, RPS26, RPL4, RPL7A, RPLP0) combined with translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) indicates high protein synthesis capacity required for rapid progenitor proliferation and differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPS17, RPS23, RPS24, RPS26: 40S ribosomal subunit proteins, foundational translational machinery
RPL4, RPL7A, RPLP0: 60S ribosomal subunit components, coordinated with 40S assembly

GAPDH: Glycolytic enzyme supporting energetic demands of active protein synthesis
UQCRH: Mitochondrial electron transport chain complex, supplying ATP for translation
YBX1: RNA binding protein regulating translational control and mRNA stability

Confirm elevated protein synthesis rates using puromycin incorporation assays. Cross-reference with S/G2-M cell cycle markers (PCNA, MKI67) to dissect whether signature reflects cycling vs. non-cycling progenitors.

functional_description: This signature reflects active chromatin remodeling and transcriptional dynamics in Pre-cDC progenitors, driven by nucleosome-associated proteins (HMGN1, HMGN2, HMGB1) and RNA-binding proteins (HNRNPA1, HNRNPA2B1, HNRNPC) that facilitate open chromatin architecture and mRNA processing. The enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23) and translation factors (PPIA) indicates elevated protein synthesis capacity typical of actively differentiating progenitors preparing for DC lineage commitment.
key_evidence: HMGN1: nucleosomal DNA binding, transcriptionally active chromatin maintenance in Pre-cDC (57% composition)

HNRNPA2B1: RNA binding protein complex with hnRNPs for splicing regulation

RPS24, RPS23: ribosomal proteins indicating elevated translation during lineage commitment
YBX1: cold shock domain protein with DNA/RNA binding in stress/differentiation response

programme_name: pDC cytotoxic maturation and plasma cell differentiation
functional_description: This signature represents activated pDC with enhanced cytotoxic effector functions and antibody-secreting cell differentiation capacity. The co-expression of GZMB (cytotoxic granule protein), JCHAIN (joining chain for polymeric immunoglobulin assembly), and IRF7 (master pDC transcription factor for Type I IFN) indicates pDC undergoing functional maturation with simultaneous acquisition of plasma cell-like secretory features.
key_evidence: LILRA4: canonical pDC-specific surface marker confirming cell-type identity
IRF7: master transcription factor for pDC function and Type I IFN production
GZMB: cytotoxic serine protease indicating activated, mature pDC phenotype

PLD4: nucleotide sensing and phagocytosis-associated nuclease in pDC

SERPINF1: serpin-family protein supporting secretory function and anti-apoptotic activity

functional_description: This signature reflects robust MHC class II antigen presentation machinery, predominantly active in both cDC1 and cDC2 populations. The coordinate upregulation of HLA-DR, HLA-DP, and HLA-DQ heterodimers with their associated chaperones (CD74, HLA-DMA/DMB) indicates enhanced capacity for exogenous antigen processing and presentation to CD4+ T cells. This represents shared dendritic cell functionality rather than cDC1-specific programming.

HLA-DPA1/DPB1: alternative MHC class II presentation pathway
HLA-DQA1/DQB1: MHC class II heterodimer components
CD74: MHC class II chaperone and trafficking regulator
HLA-DMA/DMB: peptide loading complex for class II
CPVL: antigen processing protease in endosomal pathway
CST3: cysteine protease inhibitor, regulates proteolysis
Equal cDC1/cDC2 activation (46%/45.5%): not cDC1-specific

Validation should compare cDC1-high versus cDC2-high subsets to confirm whether this reflects genuine cDC1 biology or contamination from cDC2 dominance in the activating population.

functional_description: This signature reflects cDC2 activation and maturation with enhanced antigen presentation machinery and innate immune signaling. The enrichment of HLA-DMA, CD83, and TYROBP indicates active MHC-II processing and maturation, while elevated iron metabolism (FTH1) and metabolic reprogramming (NAMPT) support increased immunological function characteristic of activated cDC2.

programme_name: cDC2 protein synthesis and metabolic activity
functional_description: This signature reflects heightened translational capacity and oxidative phosphorylation in cDC2 cells, driven by coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (40S and 60S subunits) and ATP synthase subunits. The enrichment suggests cDC2 maintain elevated protein synthetic demand and mitochondrial ATP production to support antigen presentation, cytokine production, and immune activation.

RPS17: 40S subunit ribosomal protein; component of protein synthesis apparatus required for sustained immune function
RPS24: 40S subunit ribosomal protein; elevated in cDC2 versus cDC1/pDC reflecting translational demand
RPL4: 60S large subunit ribosomal protein; supports mRNA translation for cytokine/chemokine production
RPL7A: 60S subunit component; involved in ribosome biogenesis and protein synthesis capacity

programme_name: pDC plasma cell differentiation and Type I IFN
functional_description: This signature reflects a specialized pDC subset undergoing plasma cell differentiation with concurrent Type I interferon production capacity. The co-expression of JCHAIN, MZB1, and immunoglobulin-associated genes with master pDC transcription factors (IRF7, TCF4) and pDC-specific markers (LILRA4) indicates pDC commitment to antibody-secreting cell fate while maintaining cytokine production machinery.

TCF4: E2-2 master pDC transcription factor for lineage specification

YBX1: RNA/DNA binding protein regulating translational efficiency and mRNA stability
NPM1: nucleolar shuttle protein involved in ribosome biogenesis and protein chaperoning

ANXA2, COTL1: cytoskeletal regulators consistent with progenitor morphology maintenance

This core antigen presentation machinery is constitutively expressed across cDC1, cDC2, and pre-cDC populations, reflecting the fundamental role of MHC-II-mediated CD4+ T cell activation in DC biology.

HLA-DPA1: HLA class II alpha chain; DP molecule assembly
HLA-DPB1: HLA class II beta chain; DP heterodimer maturation

HLA-DQB1: HLA class II beta chain; DQ heterodimer formation

functional_description: This signature reflects constitutive MHC-II expression and peptide-loading machinery shared across cDC1, cDC2, and pre-cDC populations. functional_description: This signature represents mature, activated pDCs with dual functionality: robust Type I interferon production (IRF7) combined with markers of plasma cell differentiation and antibody production. functional_description: This signature reflects active protein synthesis machinery coupled with MHC-II antigen presentation pathways, characteristic of metabolically active DCs engaged in antigen processing and display. The co-enrichment of ribosomal proteins, translation factors, and HLA-DM/HLA-DR components indicates simultaneous demand for de novo protein synthesis to support MHC-II molecule assembly and peptide loading.

SLC25A3: Mitochondrial phosphate transporter supporting ATP production for biosynthetic demands
ACTG1, TMSB4X: Actin dynamics supporting cytoskeletal remodelling during antigen uptake and presentation

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated basal metabolic and translational activity in DC progenitors, particularly Pre-cDC cells (60% of activating population). Pre-cDC dominance (60%): signature enriched in committed cDC progenitors over bipotent ASDC

programme_name: pDC maturation and plasma cell differentiation

functional_description: This signature represents a metabolic and translational programme characteristic of Pre-cDC progenitors, dominated by glycolytic enzymes (GAPDH, TPI1), ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS17, RPS2), and nucleotide-binding factors supporting active protein synthesis and energy metabolism. MT-CO3: Respiratory chain complex IV assembly; validates OXPHOS elevation across multiple ETC subunits

programme_name: Metabolic priming in committed cDC progenitors

MT-CO2: Mitochondrial respiration component supporting oxidative phosphorylation in energetically demanding progenitors

functional_description: This signature reflects myeloid-lineage antimicrobial and inflammatory effector functions rather than dendritic cell progenitor identity. Despite 65% Pre-cDC composition, the gene signature lacks canonical pre-cDC commitment markers (CLEC12A, PTPRS, LY86) and progenitor-defining features.

LYZ + RNASE2 + FCN1: Antimicrobial effector repertoire typical of monocytic lineage, not characteristic of DC progenitors

MNDA: Granulocyte-monocyte lineage marker, incompatible with commitment to DC lineage
Absence of CLEC12A, PTPRS, LY86, IRF8, IRF4, SPIB: Lacks canonical DC progenitor and lineage-commitment signatures
Absence of cell-cycle markers (MKI67, PCNA, TOP2A): Not consistent with actively cycling progenitors

Assess expression of CLEC12A, PTPRS, and LY86 at protein level. Evaluate FLT3/CSF1R surface expression to distinguish FLT3-dependent DC progenitors from CSF1R-dependent myeloid cells.

functional_description: This signature reflects metabolic activation and antimicrobial effector function in Pre-cDC populations, dominated by glycolytic enzymes (GAPDH, TPI1), antimicrobial peptidases (LYZ), and calcium-signaling proteins (S100A6, S100A11, ANXA2). The enrichment of HLA class II molecules (HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1) and SPI1 (PU.1, a myeloid transcription factor) indicates differentiation commitment toward functional cDC2 without cell cycle activation.

programme_name: cDC2 MHC-II antigen presentation and iron homeostasis
