TMSB4X/COTL1: Actin regulators supporting cytoskeletal remodeling and cell migration capacity in mature DCs
LGALS1: Galectin-1 mediating cell-cell interactions and immune homeostasis in mature DC populations
ATP5J2/ATP5F1/ATPIF1: Oxidative phosphorylation machinery supporting energetic demands of antigen presentation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of HLA-DQ and HLA-DP surface expression combined with CD74 and SPI1 immunofluorescence across Pre-cDC, cDC1, and cDC2 populations. RNA-seq on sorted populations with ATAC-seq to confirm SPI1 enhancer activity. Functional assays measuring antigen presentation capacity (peptide-MHC loading assays) and migration potential in maturation-gradient populations.

functional_description: This signature represents the core MHC-II antigen presentation machinery highly expressed in cDC2 (58.5% of activating cells). The coordinated upregulation of HLA-DR, HLA-DP, and HLA-DQ heterodimeric chains alongside CD74 (MHC-II chaperone) and HLA-DM peptide-loading molecules reflects the specialized capacity of cDC2 for efficient exogenous antigen processing and presentation to CD4+ T cells.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA: MHC-II alpha chain, core component of HLA-DR heterodimer essential for cDC2 antigen presentation
HLA-DRB1: MHC-II beta chain, primary HLA-DR variant in cDC2-mediated CD4+ T cell activation
HLA-DPA1 + HLA-DPB1: MHC-II DP heterodimer, important alternative MHC-II presentation pathway in professional APCs
HLA-DQA1 + HLA-DQB1: MHC-II DQ heterodimer, broadens peptide repertoire for cDC2 antigen presentation
CD74: Invariant chain and MHC-II chaperone, essential for proper folding and trafficking of MHC-II complexes
HLA-DMA + HLA-DMB: Peptide exchange factors in MHC-II loading compartments, optimize peptide-MHC-II binding
CPVL: Carboxypeptidase involved in peptide trimming during antigen processing
CST3: Cystatin C regulates cathepsin activity during endosomal antigen processing
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ surface expression on sorted cDC2 (CLEC12A+ CD1c+ CD14-low) versus cDC1 and pDC. Functional assay: assess MHC-II-restricted CD4+ T cell proliferation capacity. Confirm cDC1 exclusion by XCR1 negativity and pDC exclusion by SIGLEC-H negativity.

programme_name: HLA Class II Antigen Presentation Maturation
functional_description: This signature reflects late-stage DC maturation characterized by robust HLA class II antigen presentation machinery. The enrichment in Pre-cDC (40%) and mature cDC2 (31.5%) populations indicates activation during DC differentiation, with coordinated expression of HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, and HLA-DP heterodimeric components alongside CD74 (chaperone for class II loading). Mitochondrial electron transport genes (MT-CO2, MT-CO3) suggest elevated metabolic demand during antigen presentation function.
key_evidence: HLA-DRB1, HLA-DRA: core HLA-DR heterodimer for antigen presentation; dominant in mature cDC2
HLA-DQB1, HLA-DQA1: HLA-DQ class II molecule; cDC2-associated antigen presentation
CD74: essential MHC class II chaperone and invariant chain; mature DC hallmark
HLA-DMB, HLA-DMA: MHC class II peptide editing complex; indicates active antigen processing
HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1: HLA-DP presentation pathway; differentiation-associated upregulation
MT-CO2, MT-CO3: oxidative phosphorylation; metabolic support for antigen presentation
TMSB4X: actin dynamics; consistent with mature DC morphology and migration
CST3: cysteine protease inhibitor; protease balance in endosomal/phagosomal antigen processing
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry quantifying HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, HLA-DP surface expression intensity across Pre-cDC, cDC1, cDC2 populations; correlate with CD74 expression. Functional validation: antigen presentation assay (allogeneic MLR or peptide-MHC tetramer uptake) to confirm maturation stage. qPCR for HLA class II genes in sorted DC subsets.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein and translation machinery expression in DC progenitors, particularly Pre-cDC and Pre-pDC populations. The enrichment of ribosomal structural proteins (RPS2, RPS17, RPS23, RPS24, RPL4, RPL37A, RPLP0) and RNA-binding proteins (HNRNPA1, YBX1) indicates high translational capacity supporting active protein synthesis during progenitor differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS2, RPS23, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL4, RPLP0: core ribosomal proteins enriched in metabolically active progenitors
HNRNPA1: mRNA processing and stability regulation supporting translation
YBX1: nucleic acid binding protein regulating mRNA translation and stability
GAPDH: glycolytic enzyme reflecting metabolic activity in proliferating progenitors
HMGN1, PTMA, H3F3A: chromatin and nucleosome dynamics associated with active transcription
MT-CO2, MT-CO3: mitochondrial respiratory chain proteins supporting ATP production for anabolic processes
Pre-cDC dominance (56%): signature most active in committed cDC progenitors with high biosynthetic demand
suggested_validation: Confirm elevated ribosomal biogenesis by polysome profiling or 80S monosome enrichment; validate Pre-cDC specificity via flow cytometry sorting (CLEC12A+PTPRS+) followed by qPCR of signature genes; assess temporal dynamics during FLT3L-driven progenitor differentiation in vitro.

functional_description: This signature represents late-stage pDC development characterized by master transcriptional regulators (TCF4, IRF7) and canonical pDC identity markers (IL3RA, LILRA4). The enrichment of genes involved in immunoglobulin biology (JCHAIN, MZB1) and nucleic acid sensing pathway components (PLD4) reflects differentiation toward mature, TLR-responsive pDCs capable of robust Type I interferon production.
key_evidence: IL3RA: pDC-restricted CD123 surface marker defining pDC lineage commitment
TCF4: Master transcription factor (E2-2) essential for pDC specification and IRF7 regulation
IRF7: Central hub for Type I interferon production and pDC terminal differentiation
LILRA4: pDC-specific inhibitory receptor, highest expression in mature pDCs
PLD4: 3'-5' exonuclease with proposed role in nucleic acid sensing and pDC differentiation
JCHAIN: Immunoglobulin J-chain indicating plasmacytoid differentiation trajectory
MZB1: Proliferation regulator supporting terminal expansion of pre-pDC to pDC
PLAC8: Chromatin remodeling factor supporting transcriptional programs in differentiating pDCs
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-gating on IL3RA+LILRA4+TCF4+ cells; single-cell qPCR validation of IRF7/TCF4 co-expression; functional assay measuring IFN-β production upon TLR9 ligation in sorted high-signature pDCs versus pre-pDC populations.

functional_description: This signature represents a pre-inflammatory myeloid programme activated in cDC2 cells, characterized by abundant S100 calcium-binding proteins (S100A8/A9/A6/A12), which function as alarmins and damage-associated molecular patterns. The signature reflects enhanced lysosomal proteolysis (CTSS), pattern recognition receptor signalling (FCN1, TYROBP/DAP12), and metabolic reprogramming (NAMPT), consistent with cDC2 activation towards antimicrobial and inflammatory responses rather than steady-state antigen presentation.
key_evidence: S100A9: Alarmin and DAMP, drives myeloid recruitment and inflammatory licensing in innate immunity
S100A8: Co-expressed with S100A9 as calprotectin heterodimer; TLR4 ligand and neutrophil chemoattractant
S100A6: S100 family member; enhanced expression during myeloid cell activation
TYROBP: DAP12 adaptor protein; essential for pattern recognition receptor signalling in cDC2
FCN1: Ficolin pattern recognition receptor; complement pathway activation and pathogen sensing
CTSS: Cathepsin S; essential for MHC-II peptide processing and inflammatory response
CD14: LPS co-receptor; monocytic marker indicating myeloid inflammation state
VCAN: Versican proteoglycan; inflammatory ECM component in tissue remodeling contexts
NAMPT: NAD+ biosynthesis; supports metabolic reprogramming during immune activation
CFD: Complement factor D; alternative pathway activation supporting inflammatory responses
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain cDC2 (CD141-/CLEC12A+) with S100A8/A9 and TYROBP/DAP12; RNA-seq validation of S100A8/A9 expression in sorted cDC2 subsets; assess correlation with TLR4/TLR2 pathway activation markers (phospho-NF-κB, phospho-p38); determine if this programme is enriched in inflammatory contexts or tissue-resident cDC2 populations.

programme_name: MHC-II antigen presentation in cDC progenitors
functional_description: This signature reflects elevated MHC class II antigen presentation machinery and ribosomal protein expression, characteristic of Pre-cDC cells engaged in active protein synthesis and immunological function. The dominance of Pre-cDC (57.5%) combined with HLA-DR/DM components indicates active preparation for professional antigen-presenting capacity during cDC lineage commitment.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA: MHC class II alpha chain; core component of antigen presentation machinery enriched in Pre-cDC
HLA-DRB1: MHC class II beta chain partner; essential for peptide-MHC loading and display
CD74: MHC class II-associated chaperone (Ii chain); regulates antigen processing and presentation pathway
HLA-DMA: MHC class II peptide exchange factor; facilitates optimal peptide loading onto MHC-II
RPS2, RPS24, RPS17, RPS23, RPL4: Ribosomal proteins; indicate robust protein synthesis capacity during progenitor differentiation
LYZ: Lysozyme; antimicrobial effector molecule expressed in mature phagocytes, marks Pre-cDC functional readiness
AIF1: Calcium-binding protein; promotes myeloid cell activation consistent with cDC progenitor maturation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining for HLA-DR, CD74, and CLEC12A (Pre-cDC marker) in CD34+ bone marrow populations; validate MHC-II upregulation during FLT3L-driven cDC differentiation; compare signature expression between Pre-cDC, ASDC, and committed cDC1/cDC2 populations to confirm progenitor-specific activation pattern.

functional_description: This signature reflects active protein synthesis in pre-pDC and pDC populations, driven by constitutive ribosomal protein and translation factor expression. IRF8 co-expression indicates early lineage priming toward cDC1 fate within a predominantly pDC-committed population, suggesting a transitional state between multipotent and lineage-restricted progenitors.
key_evidence: IRF8: Strongest DC-lineage marker in signature; cDC1-associated transcription factor present in pre-pDC progenitors undergoing early lineage commitment
RPLP0, RPS23, RPL37A, RPS17, RPL4, RPL7A, RPS2: Ribosomal structural proteins collectively indicating high translational capacity essential for DC progenitor protein production
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor supporting active protein synthesis in metabolically active progenitor cells
PLD4: Exonuclease with predicted role in hematopoietic progenitor differentiation, consistent with pre-pDC developmental state
PLAC8: Predicted chromatin binding activity suggesting transcriptional regulation during pDC/cDC lineage bifurcation
Cell composition: 47.5% Pre-pDC + 42.5% pDC = 90% pDC lineage dominance with IRF8 indicating early cDC1 priming within committed progenitors
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: sort Pre-pDC (SIGLEC-H+, SPIB+, low lineage markers) and validate IRF8 protein expression by intracellular staining; qPCR quantify IRF8 and ribosomal protein mRNA in purified Pre-pDC vs mature pDC; single-cell RNA-seq trajectory analysis to map IRF8 expression kinetics during pDC→cDC1 lineage switching

functional_description: Pan-DC programme encoding the complete MHC-II presentation pathway, including chaperone-mediated peptide loading (CD74, HLA-DM), classical presentation molecules (HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, HLA-DP), and accessory factors for antigen processing. This signature spans cDC1, cDC2, and pDC equally, representing a core dendritic cell immunological function.
key_evidence: CD74: MHC-II chaperone essential for peptide loading and stability
HLA-DPA1/DPB1: HLA-DP heterodimer for MHC-II presentation
HLA-DQA1/DQB1: HLA-DQ heterodimer for MHC-II presentation
HLA-DRA/DRB1: HLA-DR heterodimer for MHC-II presentation
HLA-DMB: MHC-II peptide exchange catalyst in endosomal compartment
CPVL: Carboxypeptidase for peptide trimming during processing
CST3: Cystatin protease inhibitor regulating endosomal proteolysis
TMSB4X: Actin dynamics supporting vesicular trafficking for antigen delivery
UCP2: Mitochondrial uncoupling for ATP supply during antigen processing
DNASE1L3: Nuclease supporting immune homeostasis in presentation pathway
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry surface staining of HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, HLA-DP across cDC1/cDC2/pDC; functional MHC-II peptide presentation assay; immunofluorescence co-localisation of CD74 with HLA-II molecules in endosomal compartments

functional_description: This signature reflects metabolic adaptation and cellular stress responses in cDC2 and pre-cDC populations, driven by iron storage (FTH1), NAD+ biosynthesis (NAMPT), and polyamine catabolism (SAT1). The prominence of housekeeping genes (GAPDH, RPS2, RPS4Y1) and stress-responsive transcription factors (CEBPD, YBX1) suggests metabolic reprogramming rather than cDC2-specific differentiation or antigen presentation functions.
key_evidence: FTH1: Iron homeostasis and ferritin heavy chain—metabolic stress indicator in activated myeloid cells
NAMPT: NAD+ salvage pathway activation—energy metabolism during inflammation
CEBPD: bZIP transcription factor regulating metabolic and stress responses in myeloid lineage
STX11: Vesicular trafficking—supports protein synthesis and secretory pathway under metabolic demand
S100A6: Calcium-binding protein involved in cell proliferation and metabolic adaptation
SAT1: Polyamine catabolism regulator—metabolic marker of activated immune cells
YBX1: RNA/DNA binding protein with moonlighting roles in stress responses and translation control
TIMP1: Inflammatory marker and matrix remodelling inhibitor in activated dendritic cells
suggested_validation: This signature lacks canonical cDC2 markers (KLF4, NOTCH2, CD1C, CLEC12A, TLR4) and lineage-specific transcription factors. Validate by: (1) qPCR confirmation of FTH1, NAMPT, SAT1 across sorted cDC1/cDC2/pDC populations; (2) intracellular iron staining (Perls' staining) and NAD+ quantification; (3) assess whether signature enriches in metabolically active cDC2 subsets or stress-activated pre-cDC.

functional_description: This signature reflects differentiation of plasmacytoid dendritic cells toward antibody-secreting plasma cell fate, characterized by immunoglobulin production machinery and loss of canonical DC functions. The dominant presence of JCHAIN (IgA assembly), MZB1 (B cell maturation), combined with pDC-specific markers (LILRA4, IRF7, TCF4) suggests pDC contributing to humoral immunity through plasma cell transdifferentiation or cross-talk with B cells.
key_evidence: LILRA4: pDC-specific surface marker and master lineage determinant
IRF7: Master transcription factor for pDC identity and Type I IFN response
TCF4: E2-2 transcription factor essential for pDC development
JCHAIN: Immunoglobulin A joining chain—indicative of plasma cell/antibody secretory program
MZB1: Marks B cell/plasma cell maturation and proliferation
PLD4: Nucleic acid sensor supporting pDC-intrinsic TLR signaling
GZMB: Cytotoxic granule component suggesting activated effector pDC
87% pDC composition: dominant cell type with minimal contamination
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining (LILRA4+IRF7+ pDC vs JCHAIN+CD138+ plasma cells); single-cell transcriptomics to confirm pDC-to-plasma cell trajectory; assess IgA secretion and TLR7/9 responsiveness in sorted LILRA4+JCHAIN+ cells.

programme_name: cDC2 Lysosomal Protease and Antigen Processing
functional_description: This signature reflects cDC2-enriched lysosomal cathepsin and cysteine protease activity essential for MHC-II antigen processing and presentation. The programme combines proteolytic machinery (CTSS, CPVL, CST3) with lectin-mediated antigen uptake (CLEC7A, LGALS2) and regulatory factors controlling protease activity and inflammatory responses.
key_evidence: CTSS: lysosomal cysteine proteinase critical for peptide generation for MHC-II presentation in DC
CLEC7A: C-type lectin receptor mediating β-glucan/fungal antigen uptake in cDC2
LGALS2: galectin-2 lectin involved in lymphotoxin-α binding and immune regulation
CPVL: carboxypeptidase required for trimming peptides during antigen processing
CST3: cystatin superfamily cysteine protease inhibitor regulating lysosomal proteolysis
PSAP: saposin precursor supporting lysosomal hydrolase function in antigen-presenting cells
ZFP36L1: early response gene regulating inflammatory mRNA stability in activated DC
TMSB4X: actin regulator supporting cDC2 migration and antigen capture
CLEC9A: C-type lectin receptor distinguishing cDC1/cDC2 lineages
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of primary cDC2 (CLEC12A+CD1c+) with anti-CTSS, LGALS2, and CLEC7A; compare CTSS activity and peptide-MHC complexes between cDC2 vs cDC1 (CLEC9A+) and pDC (SIGLEC-H+); functional assays measuring antigen presentation capacity with selective protease inhibitors

functional_description: This signature reflects active cell cycle progression in Pre-cDC progenitors, characterized by upregulation of mitotic spindle proteins, microtubule dynamics, and chromatin remodeling factors. The coordinated expression of histone variants (H2AFZ, H2AFV, H3F3A), HMG box proteins involved in chromatin accessibility (HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN2), and mitotic machinery (STMN1, NUSAP1, TUBA1B, TUBB) indicates active G2/M phase progression in committed cDC progenitors.
key_evidence: STMN1: Canonical microtubule-destabilizing protein essential for mitotic spindle organization
NUSAP1: Nucleolar-spindle-associated protein critical for spindle microtubule organization during M-phase
TUBA1B, TUBB: Alpha and beta tubulin components of mitotic spindle apparatus
CKS1B: Cyclin-dependent kinase binding partner essential for cell cycle progression
HMGB1, HMGB2: HMG box proteins facilitating chromatin remodeling during active transcription in cycling cells
HMGN2: Nucleosomal protein maintaining open chromatin structure in transcriptionally active cycling cells
H2AFZ, H2AFV, H3F3A: Histone variants enriched during active chromatin dynamics in proliferating cells
ANP32B: Histone chaperone involved in nucleosome dynamics during cell cycle
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining Pre-cDC (CLEC12A+PTPRS+) with PCNA, Ki67, and phospho-histone H3 to confirm S/G2-M phase enrichment; RNA FISH for STMN1 and NUSAP1 co-expression in sorted Pre-cDC populations

functional_description: This signature represents a metabolic and housekeeping gene programme enriched in DC progenitors, particularly Pre-cDC and Pre-pDC populations. The gene set reflects active protein synthesis (RPS2, RPS17, RPS24), glycolytic metabolism (GAPDH, TPI1), mitochondrial function (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, SLC25A5), and nucleic acid binding activities (YBX1, PTMA) characteristic of metabolically active progenitor cells rather than lineage commitment signals.
key_evidence: GAPDH: Core glycolytic enzyme marking metabolically active progenitors
RPS2, RPS17, RPS24: Ribosomal proteins indicating active protein synthesis in progenitors
MT-CO2, MT-CO3: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation genes reflecting bioenergetic demands of proliferating progenitors
PTMA: DNA-binding protein with anti-apoptotic function supporting progenitor survival
YBX1: RNA/DNA binding protein involved in translational regulation and stress responses
SLC25A5: ADP/ATP transporter supporting mitochondrial energy metabolism
HMGN1: Chromatin-associated protein marking transcriptionally active euchromatic state of progenitors
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry measuring protein synthesis rates (e.g., puromycin incorporation) and mitochondrial membrane potential (JC-1 or TMRM staining) in sorted Pre-cDC and Pre-pDC populations; confirm enrichment in early progenitors versus mature DC subsets lacking this metabolic signature.

functional_description: This signature reflects enhanced lysosomal cysteine protease activity and antigen degradation pathways characteristic of cDC2s engaged in MHC-II-restricted antigen presentation. The coordinated upregulation of CTSS, CPVL, and PSAP indicates active processing of internalized antigens into peptide epitopes, while S100A8/A9 and FCN1 suggest concurrent innate immune recognition and inflammation.
key_evidence: CTSS: lysosomal cysteine protease essential for MHC-II antigen processing and peptide generation
PSAP: saposin-containing preproprotein involved in lysosomal proteolysis and lipid antigen presentation
CPVL: carboxypeptidase required for trimming processed peptide epitopes
FCN1: ficolin pattern-recognition receptor mediating complement activation and pathogen opsonisation
S100A8/S100A9: calprotectin heterodimer driving TLR4/MyD88-dependent inflammatory responses in myeloid cells
CLEC7A: Dectin-1 β-glucan receptor linking fungal recognition to cDC2 activation
IDO1: indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase supporting immunoregulatory tryptophan catabolism
LGALS2: galectin-2 lectin modulating lymphocyte interactions and immune tolerance
suggested_validation: Validate via flow cytometry measuring CTSS activity (cathepsin S substrate assay) and MHC-II-peptide complexes in cDC2-enriched subsets; confirm co-expression of S100A8/A9 calprotectin and FCN1 in inflammatory cDC2 clusters; assess correlation with IL-12B/IL-23A production in TLR-stimulated cultures.

programme_name: Myeloid differentiation and innate immune activation
functional_description: This signature reflects pre-cDC and cDC2 cells in active myeloid differentiation with enhanced innate immune effector functions. The dominant S100A family proteins (S100A6, S100A4, S100A8, S100A9) indicate calcium-dependent inflammatory signaling and antimicrobial responses, while TYROBP-mediated ITAM signaling supports pattern recognition receptor activation characteristic of developing dendritic cells.
key_evidence: S100A8/A9: Calprotectin complex - hallmark of monocytic/myeloid differentiation and innate immune activation in pre-cDC populations
S100A6/A4/A11: Calcium-binding proteins supporting pro-inflammatory cytokine production in cDC2 precursors
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor critical for TLR and FcγR signaling in developing DCs
FCN1: Ficolin-1 (ficolin-1) - innate pattern recognition molecule upregulated in monocytic DC precursors
LYZ: Lysozyme - antimicrobial effector and pro-inflammatory marker in myeloid lineage
LST1: LPS and IFN-γ-inducible membrane protein supporting DC maturation and activation
VCAN: Versican - ECM remodeling during inflammatory DC differentiation
CSTA: Cystatin A - protease inhibitor balancing inflammatory proteolysis in developing DCs
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of S100A8/A9+ co-expression on CLEC12A+ cDC2 and pre-cDC populations; single-cell qPCR confirming S100A signature enrichment in pre-cDC vs mature cDC2; functional assays measuring TLR4-induced IL-12p40 production in S100A8/A9-high cell populations

programme_name: Nuclear protein synthesis and RNA processing
functional_description: This signature reflects active nucleolar and nuclear protein synthetic machinery characteristic of proliferative progenitor states. The enrichment of hnRNPs (HNRNPA1, HNRNPA2B1, HNRNPC), HMG nucleosomal proteins (HMGN1, HMGN2, HMGB1), and ribosomal/translational factors (RPS24, YWHAE) indicates elevated transcriptional activity and protein translation in Pre-pDC and Pre-cDC populations. This programme is inconsistent with quiescent mature DC phenotypes.
key_evidence: HMGN1: nucleosomal chromatin remodelling in transcriptionally active progenitor cells
HMGN2: maintains open chromatin architecture during differentiation
HNRNPA1/HNRNPA2B1/HNRNPC: RNA-binding proteins indicating active pre-mRNA processing in progenitors
PTMA: anti-apoptotic factor supporting progenitor viability
RPS24: ribosomal protein consistent with active translation in dividing cells
HMGB1: DNA-binding protein regulating transcription in proliferative states
Pre-pDC dominance (37.5%) and Pre-cDC enrichment (29%) support progenitor identity over mature DC
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry co-staining with FLT3, SIGLEC-H, and CLEC12A surface markers on Pre-pDC/Pre-cDC sorted populations; confirm elevated ribosomal protein content and hnRNP expression by qRT-PCR in progenitors versus mature cDC1/pDC; assess correlation with cell cycle markers (Ki67) to determine if signature reflects G1/S active translation or S/G2-M cycling.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated protein synthesis capacity in pre-pDC cells, driven by coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins and translation factors. The predominance of pre-pDC (69%) and pre-pDC cycling (11.5%) activating cells indicates this programme supports the biosynthetic demands of pDC differentiation and proliferation during progenitor expansion.
key_evidence: RPS24: 40S ribosomal subunit protein; core component of translation machinery
RPL37A: 60S ribosomal subunit protein; essential for ribosome assembly and function
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor; guanine nucleotide exchange factor for aminoacyl-tRNA delivery
NPM1: Nucleophosmin; involved in ribosome biogenesis and cell proliferation regulation
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein; regulates mRNA processing in proliferating cells
GAPDH: Glycolytic enzyme; moonlighting role in protein synthesis during metabolic activation
LDHB: Lactate dehydrogenase B; supports NAD+ regeneration for glycolytic energy in biosynthetically active cells
suggested_validation: Quantify ribosome content by electron microscopy or flow cytometry (anti-RPS6 phosphorylation); measure protein synthesis rates using puromycin incorporation or O-propargyl-puromycin (OPP) labelling in FACS-sorted pre-pDC versus mature pDC; confirm elevated mRNA levels of RPS24, RPL37A, and EEF1B2 by qRT-PCR in pre-pDC populations.

functional_description: This signature represents actively cycling Pre-cDC progenitors with elevated oxidative phosphorylation and chromatin remodeling activity. The co-expression of mitochondrial electron transport genes (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND5) with cell cycle regulators (STMN1) and nuclear chromatin-associated proteins (HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN2) indicates metabolically demanding progenitors undergoing proliferation during commitment to the cDC lineage.
key_evidence: STMN1: canonical G2/M cell cycle regulator, marks cycling progenitors
MT-CO3, MT-CO2, MT-ND5: mitochondrial respiratory chain complex genes indicating high metabolic demand in proliferating Pre-cDC
HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN2: chromatin remodeling proteins associated with transcriptionally active Pre-cDC undergoing lineage commitment
TUBA1B: microtubule/mitotic spindle component, supports active cell cycle progression
PPIA: chaperone enabling rapid protein synthesis during cDC progenitor expansion
94.5% Pre-cDC composition: overwhelming enrichment in committed cDC progenitor population
suggested_validation: FACS sort Pre-cDC (Lin-CD135+CD45RA+) and validate STMN1+ cycling fraction by flow cytometry; confirm mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM/JC-1) correlates with MT-gene expression; assess CCR7 expression to confirm Pre-cDC commitment stage; perform live-cell imaging to document cell cycle kinetics

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated translational capacity and protein synthesis machinery in DC progenitors, predominantly Pre-pDC cells with concurrent Pre-cDC representation. The enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPS23, RPS24, RPL4, RPS17, RPLP0, RPL37A, RPS2) indicates active protein synthesis, consistent with metabolically active progenitor populations preparing for differentiation. Co-expression of translation factors (EEF1B2) and nucleic acid-binding proteins (YBX1, HNRNPA1, HMGN1) suggests coordinated transcriptional-translational coupling during lineage commitment.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPS24, RPL4, RPS17, RPLP0, RPL37A, RPS2: Core 40S/60S ribosomal subunit components indicating elevated global protein synthesis capacity
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor ensuring efficient aminoacyl-tRNA delivery to ribosomes
YBX1: Cold-shock domain RNA-binding protein regulating mRNA stability and translation efficiency
HMGN1: Nucleosomal DNA binder associated with transcriptionally active chromatin in progenitors
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic factor supporting progenitor survival during proliferation and differentiation
AIF1: Actin-binding, cytokine-induced protein relevant to DC activation and cytoskeletal dynamics
MT-CO2: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation marker reflecting elevated metabolic demand in active progenitors
Pre-pDC dominance (38.5%) + Pre-pDC Cycling (11.0%): Combined 49.5% of activating cells indicates biosynthetic priming in pDC-committed trajectory
suggested_validation: Validate by: (1) Flow cytometry measuring surface Pre-pDC markers (SIGLEC-H-low, CD135+, CD45RA+) co-stained with ribosomal protein immunofluorescence or puromycin incorporation assays; (2) RNA-seq comparing sorted Pre-pDC versus mature pDC for ribosomal gene expression; (3) Polysome profiling or ribosomography of Pre-pDC-enriched populations; (4) Phospho-S6 immunostaining to assess active mTORC1-driven translation in Pre-pDC subsets.

functional_description: This signature reflects a pre-cDC2/cDC2 developmental state enriched in lysosomal proteases and antimicrobial factors required for pathogen degradation and antigen processing. The programme is characterized by active autophagy machinery, calcium-binding proteins supporting intracellular signalling, and oxidative phosphorylation supporting dendritic cell maturation and migration.
key_evidence: CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease essential for MHC-II antigen processing and presentation in cDC2
LYZ: Lysozyme-mediated antibacterial immunity, particularly relevant in monocyte-derived and developing DC populations
S100A6, S100A4, S100A9, S100A11: S100 family calcium sensors regulating cytoskeletal dynamics, cell migration, and innate immune signalling in myeloid cells
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor mediating TLR and Fc receptor signalling critical for cDC2 activation
LST1: LPS-responsive membrane protein enhanced by LPS and IFN-γ, supporting pattern recognition in developing DC
GRN: Granulins with immunomodulatory properties supporting myeloid cell maturation and inflammation
MT-CO2, MT-CO3: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation supporting ATP-intensive antigen processing
CSTA: Cystatin family protease inhibitor protecting intracellular proteolysis during antigen processing
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of CTSS, LYZ and S100A4/A9 expression in sorted cDC2 vs cDC1 vs pDC; functional assays testing CTSS-dependent antigen presentation and TYROBP-mediated TLR signalling in pre-cDC and mature cDC2 populations

functional_description: This signature represents the core MHC class II antigen presentation system, predominantly activated in cDC2 (70% of top cells). The programme encompasses HLA-DR, HLA-DP, and HLA-DQ heterodimeric complexes with their associated chaperone machinery (CD74, HLA-DM), essential for professional antigen-presenting cell function and T cell activation.

HLA-DRB1: Beta chain of HLA-DR complex, primary cDC2 MHC-II presentation route
HLA-DPA1: Alpha chain of HLA-DP complex, alternative MHC-II presentation pathway
HLA-DPB1: Beta chain of HLA-DP complex, cDC2-enriched antigen presentation
HLA-DQA1: Alpha chain of HLA-DQ complex, complete MHC-II repertoire coverage
HLA-DQB1: Beta chain of HLA-DQ complex, diverse peptide presentation capability
CD74: MHC-II-associated chaperone for peptide loading and trafficking
HLA-DMA: Catalytic component of peptide exchange machinery in endosomal compartments
HLA-DMB: Non-catalytic partner of DMA complex for efficient antigen processing
CXCL16: cDC2-associated chemokine supporting Th17 differentiation and inflammatory responses
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ surface expression on CLEC12A+ cDC2 versus XCR1+ cDC1; RNA-seq or qPCR confirmation of MHC-II component co-expression in FACS-sorted cDC2; functional assays measuring peptide presentation capacity and CD4+ T cell activation by these cells

functional_description: This signature represents a dendritic cell state characterized by elevated MHC class II (HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, HLA-DP) and associated molecules, reflecting enhanced antigen presentation capacity. The co-expression of cytoskeletal regulators (TMSB4X, DYNLL1) and myeloid differentiation markers (MNDA, S100A8/A9) indicates active DC maturation, though the mixed cell-type composition suggests this may capture a transitional differentiation state rather than a single DC lineage commitment.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA: Core HLA class II alpha chain, essential for cDC2 antigen presentation function
HLA-DRB1: HLA class II beta chain, primary MHC-II heterodimer for peptide presentation
HLA-DQA1/HLA-DQB1: Alternative HLA class II presentation pathway, expressed in mature DCs
HLA-DPA1/HLA-DPB1: HLA class II DP molecules for intracellular antigen presentation
TMSB4X: Actin regulation supporting DC migration and morphological plasticity during maturation
S100A8/S100A9: Myeloid maturation markers, calcium-binding proteins in monocytic/DC differentiation
MNDA: Myeloid nuclear antigen marking granulocyte-monocyte lineage progression
CLEC9A: cDC1-enriched C-type lectin receptor supporting the 26.5% cDC1 component
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry sorting by HLA-DR intensity and CD1c/CLEC12A co-staining to validate cDC2 enrichment (target >50%); RNA-FISH for HLA-DRA/HLA-DRB1 co-localization with cDC2 markers (KLF4, NOTCH2); functional assay testing T cell stimulation capacity across the HLA-II gradient to confirm maturation state independence.

programme_name: pDC Identity and IFN Regulatory Program
functional_description: This signature defines plasmacytoid dendritic cells through core transcriptional regulators (IRF7, TCF4, SPIB) and pDC-specific surface markers (LILRA4, IL3RA), coupled with ER homeostasis machinery (DERL3, SMPD3, UGCG) supporting the specialized secretory capacity required for type I interferon production. The presence of JCHAIN and MZB1 indicates active B cell-like plasma differentiation potential or antibody-mediated responses characteristic of activated pDC.
key_evidence: IRF7: Master transcription factor for type I IFN production in pDC; essential for antiviral responses
TCF4: E2-2 transcription factor; critical pDC-lineage determinant required for pDC development and identity
SPIB: PU-box binding transcriptional activator; lymphoid-specific regulator essential for pDC differentiation
LILRA4: Canonical pDC surface marker; inhibitory immunoglobulin receptor that modulates pDC function
IL3RA: CD123 marker; defines pDC identity and hematopoietic lineage commitment
JCHAIN: Immunoglobulin J chain; indicates plasma cell-like secretory differentiation in activated pDC
MZB1: Positive regulator of cell proliferation; supports pDC expansion during immune activation
DERL3: ER-associated protein quality control; essential for managing protein load in high-secreting pDC
SMPD3: Sphingomyelinase involved in exosomal biogenesis; pDC use exosomes for IFN and antigen transfer
GZMB: Cytotoxic granule component; indicates pDC activation state and effector function
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry confirming LILRA4+ IL3RA+ IRF7+ pDC phenotype; measure IRF7 nuclear translocation and type I IFN (IFN-α/β) secretion upon TLR7/TLR9 stimulation; confirm absence of TAP1 and XCR1 to exclude cDC1 contamination.

functional_description: Pan-DC programme driving classical MHC class II antigen presentation through coordinated expression of HLA-DR, HLA-DP, and HLA-DQ heterodimers, coupled with CD74-mediated peptide loading and HLA-DM-facilitated editing. Co-expression of proteases (CPVL) and cysteine protease inhibitors (CST3) suggests coordinated endosomal processing of internalized antigens for optimal peptide generation and presentation.
key_evidence: HLA-DRB1, HLA-DRA: core MHC-II heterodimer (DR) expressed across all DC subtypes
HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1: MHC-II DP heterodimer chain components
HLA-DQA1, HLA-DQB1: MHC-II DQ heterodimer chain components
CD74: chaperone essential for MHC-II assembly, trafficking, and invariant chain peptide exchange
HLA-DMA, HLA-DMB: non-classical MHC-II molecules facilitating peptide exchange in endosomal compartments
CPVL: carboxypeptidase for C-terminal trimming of processed peptides
CST3: cysteine protease inhibitor regulating endosomal protease activity
SPI1: PU.1 transcription factor driving myeloid differentiation and MHC-II expression
cDC2 (37%) and Pre-cDC (26.5%) predominance: cell types with professional antigen presentation capacity
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry quantifying HLA-DR/DP/DQ surface expression and MFI across cDC1/cDC2/pDC; immunofluorescence co-localizing CD74 and HLA-DM in endosomal compartments; functional assay measuring peptide-MHC-II complex formation and presentation efficiency to CD4+ T cells

functional_description: This signature represents a metabolically active state characterized by elevated ribosomal proteins, translation factors, and iron metabolism supporting high protein synthesis capacity. The enrichment of RPS and RPL genes indicates robust translational machinery, while FTH1 reflects iron-dependent oxidative metabolism typical of activated dendritic cells.
key_evidence: RPS2: Core 40S ribosomal subunit protein; dominant signature component indicating active protein synthesis
RPL4, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPLP0: Large 60S ribosomal subunit proteins; collective ribosomal dominance across signature
RPS24, RPS23, RPS17: Small 40S ribosomal subunit proteins; consistent ribosomal biogenesis theme
FTH1: Iron storage and redox homeostasis; critical for dendritic cell metabolic activation
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor; supports sustained protein synthesis demands
YBX1: RNA binding protein and stress response regulator; possible translational regulation
HLA-DMA: MHC-II chaperone; modest cDC2 marker indicating antigen presentation capability
GAPDH: Glycolytic enzyme with moonlighting functions; metabolic activation marker
suggested_validation: Validate against active cDC2 transcription factor signature (KLF4, IRF4, ZEB2, NOTCH2) and cDC2-specific surface markers (CLEC12A, CD1C, FCGR2A) to confirm this represents metabolically activated cDC2. Assess ribosomal protein correlation with DC maturation markers and functional cDC2 assays (cytokine production, phagocytosis). Note: signature lacks canonical cDC2-specific transcription factors and inflammatory mediators, suggesting this captures proliferative/metabolic state rather than functional lineage identity.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated protein synthesis capacity in Pre-pDC and pDC populations, dominated by ribosomal structural proteins (RPS, RPL families) and translation elongation factors. The enrichment of nucleolar and translation machinery genes (NPM1, FBL, EEF1B2) indicates active anabolic metabolism supporting rapid progenitor proliferation and differentiation, rather than a specific lineage commitment signal.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPS23, RPS17, RPS24: Ribosomal 40S subunit proteins - housekeeping markers of translational activity
RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0: Ribosomal 60S subunit proteins - core translation machinery
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor GEF - necessary for aminoacyl-tRNA delivery
NPM1: Nucleolar protein involved in ribosome biogenesis and cell proliferation
FBL: Nucleolar snRNP component in pre-rRNA processing
GAPDH, LDHB, UQCRH: Metabolic enzymes supporting high energy demand in active progenitors
Cell composition: 38% Pre-pDC + 5% Pre-pDC Cycling dominates (43% total cycling/proliferative pDC lineage)
suggested_validation: Validate through ribosomal protein immunofluorescence and metabolic profiling (Seahorse analysis) comparing Pre-pDC vs quiescent Pre-cDC. Cross-reference with cell cycle phase distribution to confirm enrichment in S/G2-M phase Pre-pDC. Note this signature lacks lineage-determining factors (SPIB, IRF8, IRF4) and likely reflects metabolic/proliferative state rather than commitment.

functional_description: This signature reflects pDC activation toward a cytotoxic-secretory phenotype, combining canonical pDC identity (LILRA4) with granzyme-mediated cytotoxicity (GZMB) and plasma cell-like immunoglobulin secretion machinery (JCHAIN, MZB1). The inclusion of IRF7 alongside GZMB suggests activated pDC transitioning toward effector functions beyond classical Type I IFN production.
key_evidence: LILRA4: pDC-specific surface marker; master regulator of pDC function and immune modulation
IRF7: Master transcription factor for Type I IFN response and pDC terminal differentiation
GZMB: Cytotoxic serine protease atypical for canonical pDC but present in activated/differentiated pDC subsets
JCHAIN: J-chain for immunoglobulin assembly; indicates pDC transitioning toward plasma cell-like secretory phenotype
MZB1: Marginal zone B cell marker co-expressed in activated pDC with enhanced antibody secretion capacity
RGS1: Negative regulator of G-protein signaling; marks activated/emigrating dendritic cells post-stimulation
SERPINF1: Serpin with immunomodulatory function; supports pDC homeostasis and activation state
PPP1R14B: Innate immune response regulator; involved in pDC activation signaling
suggested_validation: Sort pDC (LILRA4+BST2+SIGLEC-H+) and perform flow cytometry validation: co-stain GZMB, JCHAIN, and intracellular IRF7; use IFN-β secretion assay to confirm whether GZMB+ pDC maintain Type I IFN production or represent functionally distinct activated subset; sort GZMB+/GZMB- pDC and perform RNA-seq to establish maturation trajectory.

functional_description: This signature represents a cDC2-dominant transcriptional programme centred on MHC class II antigen presentation machinery, encompassing HLA-DR, HLA-DP, and HLA-DQ heterodimer components along with the peptide-loading chaperone complex (HLA-DM, CD74). The programme reflects the core immunological function of cDC2 in exogenous antigen processing and presentation to CD4+ T cells.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA: alpha chain of HLA-DR, fundamental MHC-II heterodimer required for cDC2-mediated antigen presentation
HLA-DRB1: beta chain of HLA-DR, most abundant MHC-II variant in cDC2; strongest DC-internal discriminator
HLA-DPA1/HLA-DPB1: HLA-DP heterodimer components; alternative MHC-II presentation pathway enriched in cDC2
HLA-DQA1/HLA-DQB1: HLA-DQ heterodimer; third MHC-II pathway contributing to cDC2 antigen presentation capacity
CD74: MHC-II chaperone and peptide exchange factor; essential for loading exogenous peptides onto HLA-DR/DP/DQ
HLA-DMA/HLA-DMB: peptide-loading catalytic complex; works with CD74 to optimize MHC-II-peptide repertoire
FCGRT: neonatal Fc receptor; supports IgG-mediated immune complex uptake and cross-presentation in cDC2
LGALS2: galectin-2; lectin-type pattern recognition receptor supporting cDC2 antigen capture
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry quantifying surface HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ expression in CLEC12A+ cDC2; functional assay measuring allogeneic T cell stimulation capacity; assess CD74-dependent peptide-loading efficiency in cDC2 vs cDC1

functional_description: This signature reflects constitutive expression of the complete HLA class II antigen presentation machinery, including DR, DP, and DQ heterodimers, along with CD74 chaperone and HLA-DM peptide-loading components. The programme is characteristic of professional antigen-presenting cells with mature MHC-II processing capacity, predominantly cDC2 (42%) but also enriched in cDC1 and pre-cDC populations that all require robust MHC-II function for immune surveillance.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA: alpha chain of HLA-DR heterodimer, foundational MHC-II molecule
HLA-DRB1: beta chain of HLA-DR, most abundant MHC-II complex in cDC2
HLA-DPA1: alpha chain of HLA-DP, alternative MHC-II presentation pathway
HLA-DPB1: beta chain of HLA-DP, completes DP heterodimer for antigen presentation
CD74: essential chaperone for MHC-II assembly and peptide loading in endosomal pathway
HLA-DMA: alpha chain of HLA-DM, catalyses peptide exchange in MHC-II molecules
HLA-DMB: beta chain of HLA-DM, required for optimal peptide-MHC-II complex formation
HLA-DQA1: alpha chain of HLA-DQ, tertiary MHC-II presentation pathway
HLA-DQB1: beta chain of HLA-DQ, completes DQ heterodimer
SPI1: PU.1 transcription factor critical for myeloid differentiation and MHC-II regulation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of surface HLA-DR, HLA-DP, and HLA-DQ expression levels across cDC1/cDC2/pDC; immunofluorescence for CD74 and HLA-DM co-localisation in endosomal compartments; functional MHC-II peptide presentation assay comparing signature-positive vs negative DC subsets

functional_description: This signature reflects the canonical MHC class II antigen presentation pathway, predominantly active in cDC2 (47.5% of top activating cells) and pre-cDC precursors. The coordinated expression of HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, HLA-DP heterodimer components alongside the peptide-loading chaperone CD74 and HLA-DM catalytic molecules indicates active antigen processing and presentation to CD4+ T cells. Elevated ribosomal proteins suggest high translational capacity supporting sustained MHC-II production.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA: alpha chain of HLA-DR, primary MHC-II molecule on cDC2
HLA-DRB1: beta chain of HLA-DR, obligate partner for functional presentation
CD74: invariant chain and peptide-loading chaperone essential for MHC-II maturation
HLA-DMA/HLA-DMB: catalytic DM complex mediating peptide exchange in endosomal compartments
HLA-DPA1/HLA-DPB1: alternative MHC-II heterodimer with tissue-specific presentation capacity
HLA-DQA1/HLA-DQB1: third MHC-II family member enabling diverse epitope presentation
RPS2/RPS17/RPL4: elevated ribosomal proteins supporting high protein synthesis rate for MHC-II production
SPI1: PU.1 transcription factor required for myeloid lineage commitment and antigen-presenting cell development
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry quantifying HLA-DR, HLA-DQ surface expression and CD74 intracellular levels in sorted cDC2 vs cDC1; functional assay measuring antigen presentation capacity via CFSE-labeled CD4+ T cell proliferation; RNA-seq validation of coordinated HLA locus expression in cDC2-enriched populations

functional_description: This signature reflects robust MHC class II antigen presentation machinery in cDC2 dendritic cells, dominated by HLA-DQ and HLA-DP heterodimers alongside canonical HLA-DR components. The high representation of ATP synthase subunits indicates elevated metabolic activity supporting sustained antigen processing and presentation capacity.
key_evidence: HLA-DQA1: Core HLA-DQ alpha chain essential for MHC-II heterodimer formation and peptide presentation
HLA-DQB1: Obligate HLA-DQ beta chain partner for MHC-II assembly
HLA-DRA: Canonical HLA-DR alpha chain required for HLA-DR-peptide complexes
HLA-DRB1: HLA-DR beta chain, primary MHC-II presenting molecule in professional APCs
HLA-DPB1: HLA-DP beta chain for alternative MHC-II presentation pathway
HLA-DPA1: HLA-DP alpha chain partner enabling HLA-DP presentation
ATP5A1, ATP5B, ATP5F1, ATP5J2, ATP5G3: Oxidative phosphorylation components supporting metabolic demands of antigen presentation
TMSB4X: Cytoskeletal regulator supporting dendritic cell morphology and migration
FOSB: AP-1 family transcription factor potentially involved in inflammatory responses and antigen presentation regulation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining for HLA-DQ and HLA-DP surface expression on KLF4+CLEC12A+ cDC2 versus cDC1; functional assays measuring peptide presentation capacity via CFSE-labeled T cell proliferation with HLA-DQ/DP blocking antibodies; metabolic profiling via seahorse analysis of ATP production rates.

functional_description: This signature represents activated plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDC) engaged in type I interferon production and functional maturation. The programme is characterized by expression of the master pDC transcription factor IRF7, pDC-specific surface markers (LILRA4, IL3RA), and genes supporting antibody secretion and cytotoxic function, indicating pDC differentiation towards an effector phenotype.
key_evidence: IRF7: Master transcription factor for type I IFN production in pDC, essential for TLR7/9-mediated antiviral responses
LILRA4: pDC-restricted inhibitory receptor that modulates pDC immune activation and maturation
TCF4: Essential E2-2 transcription factor required for pDC lineage specification and identity maintenance
IL3RA: CD123 surface marker defining pDC identity and critical for pDC development
JCHAIN: Suggests pDC differentiation towards antibody-secreting plasma cell phenotype (IgA production)
GZMB: Cytotoxic granule protein indicating pDC functional maturation and cytotoxic capability
SERPINF1: Secreted protein supporting immunological microenvironment, consistent with activated pDC phenotype
MZB1: Positive regulator of cell proliferation in pDC maturation context
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry confirming pDC identity (SIGLEC-H+, BST2+, LILRA4+, IL3RA+) with intracellular IRF7 staining and type I IFN production assays (qRT-PCR for IFN-α/β, or protein quantification). Assess GZMB and JCHAIN expression by flow; validate antibody secretion capacity to distinguish terminal pDC differentiation stage.

programme_name: pDC Type I IFN Production and Maturation
functional_description: This signature reflects activated plasmacytoid dendritic cells with enhanced Type I interferon production capacity and secretory-lysosomal effector functions. The co-expression of IRF7 (master regulator of Type I IFN), LILRA4 (pDC-specific surface marker), and cytotoxic/secretory mediators (GZMB, PLD4) indicates pDCs transitioning toward mature, antiviral effector states with both innate immune activation and potential cytotoxic capability.
key_evidence: IRF7: Master transcription factor for Type I interferon production; hallmark of activated pDCs
LILRA4: Canonical pDC-restricted surface marker essential for pDC identification
GZMB: Serine protease enabling pDC cytotoxic function during viral responses
PLD4: pDC-enriched nuclease involved in TLR-mediated cytokine regulation
JCHAIN: J-chain protein linking to secretory IgA responses; indicates plasma cell-like secretory capacity
MZB1: Marginal zone B cell marker; likely reflects cross-talk with B cell compartment or pDC-B cell clusters
SERPINF1: Secreted protease inhibitor supporting anti-inflammatory pDC programming
ITM2C, DERL3, SMPD3, UGCG, CLIC3: ER-resident and endosomal processing genes supporting enhanced secretory pathway activity
Cell composition 98% pDC: Strongly validates pDC-dominant signature with minimal cDC contamination
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry confirming LILRA4+ SIGLEC-H+ pDCs co-expressing IRF7, GZMB, and intracellular Type I IFN (IFN-α/β). RT-qPCR validation of IRF7, PLD4, and GZMB expression. Functional assays measuring Type I IFN secretion capacity and cytotoxic granule content in sorted activated pDCs.

functional_description: This signature represents the core MHC class II antigen presentation machinery, prominently expressed in cDC2 (56% of activating cells). The co-expression of HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, and HLA-DP heterodimers alongside CD74 (invariant chain) and HLA-DM peptide-loading chaperones indicates specialised professional antigen-presenting cell function characteristic of cDC2.
key_evidence: HLA-DRB1: Central HLA-DR β-chain; core cDC2 MHC-II molecule
HLA-DRA: HLA-DR α-chain partner; constitutive cDC2 expression
CD74: Invariant chain chaperone for class II loading; essential for DC function
HLA-DPA1/HLA-DPB1: HLA-DP heterodimer; alternative MHC-II pathway in cDC2
HLA-DQA1/HLA-DQB1: HLA-DQ heterodimer; complementary cDC2 presentation axis
HLA-DMA/HLA-DMB: Peptide exchange factors; optimise antigen presentation
CXCL16: Chemokine for T-cell recruitment post-antigen presentation
CST3: Cysteine protease inhibitor; intracellular processing control
FCGRT: IgG Fc receptor; bridging humoral-cellular immunity
FTH1: Iron storage; support metabolic demands of professional APCs
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry co-staining HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, HLA-DP with cDC2 markers (CLEC12A, CD1c, KLF4) and confirm absence of cDC1 (XCR1-) and pDC (SIGLEC-H-) markers. Perform RNA-seq comparison of cDC2 vs cDC1 to confirm MHC-II enrichment specificity.

programme_name: Metabolic priming in committed cDC progenitors
functional_description: This signature reflects enhanced glycolytic and oxidative stress response capacity in Pre-cDC and cDC2 populations, driven by upregulation of core metabolic enzymes and calcium-binding proteins. The dominance of housekeeping metabolic genes (GAPDH, TPI1, PKM, TALDO1) coupled with S100 family calcium sensors and antioxidant machinery (GSTP1, FTH1) suggests metabolic priming for increased biosynthetic demand and redox regulation during cDC commitment and differentiation.
key_evidence: S100A4: Calcium-binding cytoskeletal regulator enriched in committed Pre-cDC (47.5% of activating population), supporting cellular plasticity and migration during lineage commitment
GAPDH: Core glycolytic enzyme indicating heightened metabolic flux in differentiating cDC progenitors relative to mature populations
PKM: Glycolytic pyruvate kinase suggesting sustained ATP generation for biosynthetic and signaling demands during Pre-cDC expansion
TALDO1: Non-oxidative pentose phosphate pathway enzyme supporting nucleotide synthesis for proliferating Pre-cDC progenitors
FTH1: Iron storage and antioxidant response, critical for managing oxidative stress during myeloid differentiation
GSTP1: Phase II detoxification enzyme indicating redox priming in metabolically active progenitors
COTL1: Actin-binding protein and 5-lipoxygenase interactor linking cytoskeletal dynamics to eicosanoid signaling in activated progenitors
YBX1: RNA/DNA binding protein regulating translation and stress response, supporting metabolic adaptation
suggested_validation: Validate by: (1) metabolic profiling (Seahorse) comparing Pre-cDC vs mature cDC1/cDC2 glycolysis/OXPHOS rates; (2) flow cytometry for S100A4 surface/intracellular levels on sorted Pre-cDC and ASDC; (3) assess FTH1/ferritin iron content in progenitors; (4) quantify ROS levels and GSTP1 activity in committed vs bipotent progenitors to confirm redox priming model.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated metabolic and protein synthesis activity in Pre-cDC progenitors, characterized by enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPS23, RPS24), mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation genes (MT-CO2, MT-CO3), and nuclear/chromatin-associated proteins. The programme indicates heightened bioenergetic demand and translational capacity consistent with active progenitor expansion prior to terminal cDC differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPS24: ribosomal structural proteins indicating active protein synthesis
MT-CO2, MT-CO3: mitochondrial electron transport chain components reflecting elevated oxidative metabolism
PPIA: peptidyl-prolyl isomerase supporting protein folding during high translation
HMGB1, HMGN1, H3F3A: chromatin remodeling proteins associated with transcriptionally active progenitor state
PTMA: anti-apoptotic factor protecting expanding progenitor population
YBX1: nucleic acid binding protein regulating both transcription and translation
Pre-cDC composition (75%) with minor cycling progenitor enrichment (8.5%) validates progenitor-specific signature
suggested_validation: Quantify mitochondrial mass (TMRM staining) and protein synthesis rate (puromycin incorporation) in Pre-cDC versus mature cDC1/cDC2; perform seahorse metabolic profiling to confirm enhanced OXPHOS dependency in Pre-cDC subset

programme_name: pDC Type I IFN Production and Maturation
functional_description: This signature represents activated plasmacytoid dendritic cells characterized by interferon regulatory factor (IRF7, IRF8) expression and cytotoxic effector molecule production (GZMB). The programme integrates pDC-defining markers (LILRA4, PLD4) with Type I interferon response machinery and plasma cell-like features (JCHAIN, MZB1), reflecting pDC terminal differentiation and heightened antiviral immunity.
key_evidence: IRF7: Master transcription factor for Type I IFN production in pDC
LILRA4: Canonical pDC-specific surface marker and immune modulator
GZMB: Cytotoxic granule serine protease indicating pDC activation and effector function
TCF4: E2-2 transcription factor essential for pDC lineage commitment and IRF7 regulation
IRF8: IRF family member supporting Type I IFN response and DC differentiation
PLD4: pDC-enriched nucleic acid sensor supporting innate immune activation
JCHAIN: Plasma cell marker indicating pDC transition toward antibody-secreting phenotype
MZB1: Proliferation regulator associated with pDC differentiation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry confirming 99.5% pDC enrichment (SIGLEC-H+, CD123+, LILRA4+); quantify IRF7/TCF4 protein localization by immunofluorescence; measure Type I IFN (IFNα/β) secretion by ELISA; validate GZMB expression as pDC activation marker in TLR7/9 stimulation assays

programme_name: Progenitor chromatin remodelling and RNA processing
functional_description: This signature represents active chromatin remodelling and RNA metabolism in DC progenitors, particularly Pre-cDC and Pre-pDC populations. The enrichment of nucleosome-associated proteins (HMGN1/2, HMGB1/2, H2AFZ/V/Y) indicates transcriptionally permissive chromatin architecture, while SR-protein splicing factors (SRSF3, HNRNPA1/A2B1) support dynamic pre-mRNA processing required for progenitor differentiation.
key_evidence: HMGN1: Nucleosome-binding protein maintaining open chromatin in transcriptionally active regions
HMGN2: Co-factor with HMGN1 for chromatin accessibility in differentiating progenitors
HMGB1: Non-histone DNA-binding protein regulating transcription and chromatin organisation
SRSF3: SR-family splicing factor enabling alternative splicing during DC lineage commitment
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein coordinating pre-mRNA processing in proliferating progenitors
H2AFZ: Histone variant associated with active promoters in transitional cells
STMN1: Microtubule-destabilising protein supporting cell cycle progression in Pre-pDC Cycling
ANP32B: Histone chaperone facilitating chromatin dynamics during differentiation
suggested_validation: Validate through ATAC-seq to confirm open chromatin at progenitor-specific loci; use RNA-seq to assess splicing pattern dynamics across Pre-cDC/Pre-pDC populations; correlate STMN1 expression with cell cycle phase to confirm cycling progenitor enrichment (16.5% Pre-pDC Cycling in top-200)

programme_name: cDC2 MHC-II antigen presentation and lysosomal processing
functional_description: This signature reflects the core antigen presentation and processing machinery of cDC2 cells, centered on MHC class II expression (HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1) and lysosomal proteolysis (CTSS, CPVL) required for peptide generation and loading. The elevated expression of pattern recognition receptors (CLEC7A, TYROBP) and metabolic/immunological support genes (NAMPT, FTH1, PSAP, LGALS2) indicates active antigen uptake and processing capacity typical of tissue-resident cDC2 specialization.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA: Core MHC-II alpha chain; constitutively high in cDC2
HLA-DRB1: Core MHC-II beta chain; major antigen presentation molecule
CTSS: Lysosomal cathepsin S; essential for MHC-II peptide loading
CPVL: Carboxypeptidase; processes antigens for MHC-II presentation
HLA-DPA1: MHC-II alpha chain alternative; supports presentation capacity
HLA-DPB1: MHC-II beta chain alternative; diversifies presented peptide repertoire
CLEC7A: C-type lectin receptor; pattern recognition in cDC2
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor; signaling from CLRs and Fc receptors
PSAP: Saposin processing; supports lysosomal antigen degradation
LGALS2: Galectin-2; immunomodulatory lectin in cDC2
NAMPT: NAD biosynthesis; metabolic support for active APCs
FTH1: Iron storage; manages redox stress in antigen-processing cells
FCGRT: IgG binding; supports immune complex processing
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: confirm HLA-DR+, CD1c+, CLEC7A+ phenotype and validate CTSS/CPVL co-expression. Functional assay: measure antigen presentation capacity and lysosomal processing efficiency in FACS-sorted cells. Compare with cDC1 (XCR1+, CLEC9A+) which lacks this MHC-II-focused signature.

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened protein synthesis and nucleoprotein homeostasis in DC progenitors, particularly Pre-pDC and cycling Pre-pDC populations. The enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPL4, RPLP0), RNA-binding proteins (HNRNPA1, SRSF3), and nucleosome-associated factors (HMGN1, HMGN2, HMGB1) indicates active transcriptional remodeling and translational capacity required for progenitor proliferation and differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPL4, RPLP0: ribosomal structural proteins indicate elevated protein synthesis capacity in proliferating progenitors
HNRNPA1, SRSF3: pre-mRNA processing and splicing factors support active transcriptional programs
HMGN1, HMGN2, HMGB1: chromatin remodeling proteins associated with transcriptionally active progenitor state
PTMA, ANP32B: histone chaperones and apoptotic regulators reflect chromatin dynamics during progenitor expansion
ACTG1: cytoskeletal actin required for cell motility and morphological changes in differentiating progenitors
SLC25A5: mitochondrial ADP/ATP transporter supports energetic demands of active synthesis
Pre-pDC (40%) and Pre-pDC Cycling (24%) co-dominance: cycling progenitors require elevated biosynthetic machinery
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry measuring HNRNPA1, HMGB1 protein levels in sorted Pre-pDC and Pre-pDC Cycling populations; confirm elevated protein synthesis rate via pulse-chase with O-propargyl-puromycin (OPP); assess concurrent FLT3-signaling activation (pSTAT3, pAKT) as mechanistic driver of anabolic progenitor state.

functional_description: This signature represents an early myeloid differentiation and innate immune activation program enriched in pre-cDC and immature cDC2 populations. The signature is dominated by S100 calcium-binding proteins (S100A8/A9/A6/A4/A11/A12) and myeloid pattern recognition receptors that drive antimicrobial responses and pro-inflammatory signaling, rather than mature antigen presentation functions typical of fully differentiated cDC2.
key_evidence: S100A9: Calprotectin component; myeloid differentiation and innate immune activation marker
S100A8: Calprotectin partner; neutrophil/monocyte lineage maturation and inflammation
VCAN: Versican; extracellular matrix remodeling during immune cell extravasation and tissue infiltration
FCN1: Ficolin-1; pattern recognition receptor for bacterial PAMP detection and complement activation
TYROBP: DAP12 adaptor; ITAM-based signaling for myeloid receptor activation
CD14: LPS co-receptor; defines monocyte-like, pre-cDC phenotype over mature cDC2
MNDA: Myeloid nuclear differentiation antigen; myeloid lineage commitment marker
LYZ: Lysozyme; antimicrobial effector in myeloid cells
RNASE2: Ribonuclease A family; antimicrobial ribonuclease activity
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry co-expression of S100A9/A8 with CD14 and CLEC12A in pre-cDC and immature cDC2 populations; confirm absence of mature cDC2 markers (NOTCH2 target genes, KLF4, IRF4); assess temporal dynamics during in vitro cDC2 differentiation from hematopoietic progenitors.

programme_name: pDC Identity and Type I IFN Priming
functional_description: This signature represents mature plasmacytoid dendritic cells with activated transcriptional programmes for Type I interferon production and antigen presentation. The module is characterized by master pDC transcription factors (TCF4, IRF7, IRF8) and pDC-specific surface markers (LILRA4), alongside secretory machinery components supporting robust interferon response capacity.
key_evidence: TCF4: Master transcription factor (E2-2) essential for pDC lineage specification and IRF7 regulation
IRF7: Central regulator of Type I IFN production, signature gene of activated pDC
LILRA4: pDC-specific surface marker with direct lineage-defining expression pattern
IRF8: Co-factor with IRF7 in pDC differentiation and IFN-beta production
PLD4: pDC-enriched nucleotide sensor and Type I IFN pathway regulator
JCHAIN: Immunoglobulin component indicating B-cell-like secretory capacity in pDC
GZMB: Cytotoxic granule protein suggesting pDC maturation and activation state
MZB1: Proliferation control marker consistent with activated pDC population
SSR4: ER translocon component supporting high-throughput Type I IFN synthesis
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining for LILRA4+/TCF4+/IRF7+ cells with Type I IFN production assay (pSTAT1/pSTAT3); single-cell RT-qPCR for IFNA/IFNB expression; chromatin accessibility analysis (ATAC-seq) at TCF4 and IRF7 binding sites

functional_description: This signature represents differentiation of pDC toward plasma cell-like states, characterized by activation of TCF4 (master pDC transcription factor) alongside immunoglobulin production machinery (JCHAIN, IGHM) and secretory pathway components. The presence of MZB1, SSR4, and DERL3 indicates endoplasmic reticulum stress responses and protein secretion pathways typical of antibody-secreting cells derived from pDC.
key_evidence: TCF4: Master transcription factor for pDC identity and IFN response; validates pDC origin
JCHAIN: Joining chain for polyimmunoglobulin assembly; indicates Ig production capacity unique to differentiating pDC
IGHM: IgM heavy chain expression; confirms plasma cell differentiation pathway
MZB1: Marginal zone B cell protein involved in plasma cell proliferation and differentiation
SSR4: ER translocon component; supports massive secretory protein synthesis during differentiation
DERL3: ER-resident derlin; involved in ERAD during plasma cell ER stress response
PPP1R14B: Innate immune regulator; maintains pDC signaling during transition
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of CD123+BST2+ cells co-expressing TCF4 and CD19/CD20, combined with ELISA/ELISpot for IgM and Type I IFN secretion to confirm plasma cell differentiation capability of activated pDC in this signature.

functional_description: This signature reflects the core antigen-presenting machinery of cDC2, characterized by comprehensive MHC-II expression across all three classical heterodimeric pathways (DR, DQ, DP). The dominant representation of CD74 and HLA-DM components indicates active loading and presentation of exogenous antigens, essential for cDC2-mediated T cell priming.
key_evidence: CD74: MHC-II chaperone and invariant chain, critical for antigen loading and trafficking; highest ranking gene
HLA-DRA: MHC-II α-chain; paired with DRB1 for conventional antigen presentation
HLA-DRB1: MHC-II β-chain partner; constitutively expressed on cDC2
HLA-DMA/DMB: Peptide-loading complex for MHC-II in endosomal compartments
HLA-DQA1/DQB1: Alternative MHC-II presentation pathway, cDC2-restricted
HLA-DPA1/DPB1: Third MHC-II pathway, consistent with cDC2 phenotype
GRN: Granulins support immune activation and antigen presentation contexts
CST3: Cystatin regulates proteolytic processing during antigen handling
TMSB4X: Actin dynamics support dendritic processes and antigen sampling
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, HLA-DP surface protein expression on cDC2 (CLEC12A+CD1c+CD14-) vs cDC1 and pDC; functional assay of antigen uptake and presentation capacity using fluorescent model antigens; assess CD74 localization by immunofluorescence in early endosomes.

functional_description: This signature defines mature plasmacytoid dendritic cells with activated interferon response pathways. The programme combines master pDC transcription factors (IRF7, TCF4) with pDC-specific surface markers (LILRA4) and reflects the characteristic secretory capacity of pDCs through plasma cell-related genes (JCHAIN, MZB1).
key_evidence: IRF7: Master transcription factor for Type I interferon production in pDCs; essential for pDC antiviral response
TCF4: Master regulator of pDC identity and differentiation; key E2-2 transcription factor for pDC specification
LILRA4: pDC-restricted surface marker; immunoglobulin-like receptor modulating pDC immune function
JCHAIN: Immunoglobulin-associated protein reflecting pDC's high immunoglobulin secretion capacity
MZB1: Plasma cell maturation factor indicating pDC transition to antibody-secreting phenotype
PLD4: Nucleotide sensing enzyme involved in pDC TLR7/9 signalling and cytokine production
GZMB: Cytotoxic granule component reflecting activated/mature pDC state
C12orf75: pDC-associated gene with elevated expression in interferon-activated states
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation: confirm LILRA4+SIGLEC-H+BST2+ phenotype; measure IRF7 protein and nuclear localisation; assess Type I IFN production (IFNα/β) by intracellular cytokine staining in signature-high vs signature-low pDCs

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein and translation factor expression in Pre-pDC cells, indicating high protein synthesis capacity. The dominance of Pre-pDC (71.5%) among activating cells suggests these progenitors require robust translational machinery to support differentiation and survival during early pDC lineage commitment.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS2, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL4, RPL7A: ribosomal structural proteins comprising 40S and 60S subunits, indicating active translation
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor mediating aminoacyl-tRNA delivery, essential for protein synthesis efficiency
RPLP0: ribosomal stalk protein component required for ribosome function
NPM1: nucleolar phosphoprotein involved in ribosome biogenesis and cell proliferation support
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein regulating mRNA processing and stability
ACTG1: structural actin isoform supporting cellular architecture during active differentiation
GPX1, LDHB: metabolic enzymes (antioxidant and glycolytic) supporting high-demand anabolic state
suggested_validation: Compare ribosomal protein expression across Pre-pDC, mature pDC, and Pre-cDC by flow cytometry using S6 ribosomal protein phosphorylation (p-S6) as a proxy for translational activity. Validate with bulk RNA-seq or qPCR on sorted Pre-pDC subsets. Investigate whether this translational signature correlates with FLT3L stimulation or proliferative state in Pre-pDC Cycling cells.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) coupled with active protein synthesis, indicating high metabolic demand and biosynthetic capacity across DC subtypes. The enrichment spans ATP synthase subunits (ATP5A1, ATP5B, ATP5C1, ATP5F1, ATP5G1, ATP5G3, ATP5J2, ATPIF1) and ribosomal proteins (RPS26, RPS23, RPS17, RPL4, RPLP0), characteristic of metabolically active, non-cycling DCs maintaining robust antigen presentation machinery.
key_evidence: ATP5A1: Core ATP synthase F1 subunit, essential for OXPHOS
ATP5B: ATP synthase F1 beta subunit, rate-limiting for oxidative respiration
ATP5C1: ATP synthase F1 gamma subunit, catalytic core component
ATP5G1/ATP5G3: ATP synthase F0 membrane subunits, proton gradient coupling
ATPIF1: ATP synthase inhibitor, regulates OXPHOS efficiency
RPS26/RPS23/RPS17: 40S ribosomal proteins supporting active translation
RPL4/RPLP0: 60S ribosomal proteins for complete ribosomal function
PSMA2: 20S proteasome subunit, protein quality control linked to OXPHOS
suggested_validation: Perform mitochondrial stress test (Seahorse) measuring oxygen consumption rate in sorted cDC1/cDC2/pDC; correlate ATP5A1/B protein levels with mitochondrial mass (MitoTracker); assess ribosome biogenesis by 4EU incorporation; verify signature correlates with non-cycling, mature DC states rather than progenitors.

functional_description: This signature reflects enhanced oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial ATP synthesis coupled with cytoskeletal remodeling, characteristic of metabolically active Pre-cDC progenitors. The enrichment of ATP synthase subunits (ATP5A1, ATP5B, ATP5C1, ATP5F1, ATP5G3, ATP5J2, ATPIF1) indicates elevated energy demands during progenitor proliferation and differentiation, while S100A4/A6 and TMSB4X support actin dynamics required for cell migration and morphological plasticity.
key_evidence: ATP5A1, ATP5B, ATP5C1, ATP5F1, ATP5G3, ATP5J2: mitochondrial ATP synthase complex subunits indicating oxidative metabolism
S100A4, S100A6: calcium-binding proteins regulating cytoskeletal dynamics and cell motility
TMSB4X: actin-sequestering protein controlling cytoskeletal remodeling during progenitor migration
Pre-cDC dominance (56.5%): signature enriched in committed cDC progenitors with high metabolic activity
RPS26, HNRNPA1: ribosomal and RNA-binding proteins supporting active translation in proliferating cells
ATPIF1: ATP synthase inhibitor regulating mitochondrial function during stress conditions
suggested_validation: Perform seahorse mitochondrial stress testing on sorted Pre-cDC vs mature cDC populations; validate ATP5 subunit protein expression via flow cytometry; assess S100A4/TMSB4X localization during FLT3L-driven progenitor differentiation to confirm metabolic priming signature

functional_description: This signature captures active cell cycle progression and metabolic reprogramming in cycling pDC progenitors. The enrichment of S/G2-M phase genes (STMN1, TYMS, DUT) combined with polyamine biosynthesis (ODC1) and protein synthesis machinery (RPS23, RPS2, EEF1B2) reflects the anabolic demands of proliferating pre-pDC, consistent with the 30.5% Pre-pDC Cycling composition.
key_evidence: STMN1: Canonical microtubule destabilization during cell cycle progression in cycling progenitors
TYMS: dTMP synthesis essential for DNA replication in S-phase pDC precursors
DUT: dUTP hydrolysis maintains nucleotide pools during rapid DNA synthesis
ODC1: Polyamine biosynthesis supports proliferation and differentiation in myeloid progenitors
RPS23/RPS2/EEF1B2: Translational machinery upregulation concurrent with high protein synthesis demand
MARCKSL1: Cytoskeletal reorganization supporting mitotic progression
PTMA: Nuclear factor protecting cycling cells from apoptosis during proliferation stress
suggested_validation: Validate with PCNA, MKI67, and CCNB1 co-expression; perform cell cycle phase enrichment analysis; confirm pre-pDC lineage with SIGLEC-H and SPIB expression patterns in cycling vs quiescent subsets

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated protein synthesis and translational capacity in DC progenitors, predominantly Pre-cDC and Pre-pDC populations. The enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPS2, RPL37A, RPLP0), translation factors (EEF1B2), and RNA-binding proteins (HNRNPA1, HNRNPC) indicates active translation during progenitor expansion. The co-expression with oxidative stress management (GPX1) and chromatin remodeling factors (HMGN1) suggests metabolic support for differentiation-committed progenitors.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS2, RPL37A, RPLP0: Core ribosomal structural proteins indicating high translational demand
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor required for active protein synthesis
HNRNPA1, HNRNPC: RNA-binding proteins coordinating pre-mRNA processing during active transcription
GPX1: Oxidative stress management compatible with high metabolic activity in differentiating progenitors
HMGN1: Nucleosomal remodeling associated with transcriptionally active chromatin in committed progenitors
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic and transcriptional regulator supporting progenitor survival during differentiation
ACTG1, GAPDH: Metabolic and cytoskeletal housekeeping genes supporting active cellular processes
suggested_validation: Validate via: (1) Ribosome profiling or polysome analysis in sorted Pre-cDC and Pre-pDC populations; (2) Protein synthesis rate assays (puromycin incorporation); (3) Flow cytometry quantifying ribosomal protein content across progenitor subsets; (4) Confirm Pre-cDC/Pre-pDC enrichment via surface markers (CLEC12A+PTPRS+ for Pre-cDC; SIGLEC-H+ for Pre-pDC)

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated metabolic and cytoskeletal activity in cDC2 and pre-cDC populations, dominated by ribosomal proteins (RPS26, RPS17, RPS24, RPL4, RPS23) and ATP synthase subunits (ATP5A1, ATP5B, ATP5F1, ATP5G1, ATP5G3, ATP5J2) indicating high protein synthesis capacity and oxidative ATP production. The inclusion of actin-regulatory proteins (TMSB4X, COTL1) and FOSB suggests active cytoskeletal remodeling supporting dendritic cell differentiation and migration.
key_evidence: RPS26, RPS17, RPS24, RPL4, RPS23: ribosomal proteins indicating translational capacity required for pre-cDC to cDC2 maturation
ATP5A1, ATP5B, ATP5F1, ATP5G1, ATP5G3, ATP5J2: ATP synthase complex components reflecting high metabolic demand in differentiating DCs
TMSB4X: actin-sequestering protein essential for DC morphogenesis and migration
COTL1: F-actin binding protein supporting cytoskeletal dynamics in myeloid differentiation
FOSB: immediate early gene indicating transcriptional activation during DC maturation
51% cDC2 composition with 27.5% pre-cDC: signature enriched in developmental transition stages
suggested_validation: Validate with functional assays measuring ATP production, protein synthesis rates (pulse-chase labeling), and F-actin organization (phalloidin staining) in sorted cDC2 vs cDC1. Confirm elevated oxidative phosphorylation via real-time respirometry (Seahorse assay) and correlate FOSB expression with DC maturation markers (HLA-DR upregulation, CD86).

functional_description: This signature reflects robust MHC class II antigen presentation machinery in Pre-cDC and cDC2 cells, with enrichment of CD74 and complete HLA class II heterodimer components (HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DM). The transcriptional profile indicates mature antigen-processing capacity in committed cDC lineage progenitors undergoing terminal differentiation.
key_evidence: CD74: MHC-II chaperone and invariant chain, essential for class II antigen presentation and trafficking
HLA-DRA/HLA-DRB1: HLA-DR heterodimer alpha and beta chains, primary MHC-II complex for antigen presentation
HLA-DMA/HLA-DMB: HLA-DM peptide exchange catalysts, facilitate loading of antigens onto MHC-II
HLA-DPA1/HLA-DPB1: HLA-DP heterodimer components, alternative MHC-II pathway for antigen presentation
TMSB4X: Actin regulation supporting cytoskeletal dynamics in differentiating cDC cells
CST3: Cysteine protease inhibitor involved in antigen processing and proteolytic regulation
HMGB2: Chromatin remodeling protein supporting transcriptional activity in differentiated progenitors
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: validate CD74, HLA-DR, HLA-DP surface expression on Pre-cDC and cDC2; qPCR confirmation of HLA gene module expression; ATAC-seq to confirm open chromatin at MHC-II loci in Pre-cDC subset

functional_description: This signature marks activated plasmacytoid dendritic cells engaged in antiviral Type I interferon production and maturation.
