The module combines master pDC identity markers (LILRA4, IL3RA), the central Type I IFN transcriptional regulator (IRF7), and specialized secretory/endosomal machinery required for sustained interferon responses and cytotoxic effector functions.
key_evidence: IRF7: Master transcription factor for Type I interferon production, defining pDC antiviral response
LILRA4: Canonical pDC-restricted surface marker, immunoglobulin-like receptor modulating pDC function
IL3RA: CD123 pDC-specific surface marker essential for pDC development and IL-3 responsiveness
GZMB: Granzyme B for cytotoxic effector function during pDC-mediated antiviral response
JCHAIN: J-chain protein indicating active immunoglobulin secretion and plasma cell-like differentiation
PLD4: Nucleotide sensing enzyme involved in phagocytosis and innate immune cytokine regulation
IRF8: Co-regulator of pDC transcriptional program alongside IRF7 and SPIB
DERL3: ER protein quality control supporting massive protein synthesis during IFN production
MZB1: Positive regulator of cell proliferation in activated pDC population
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: sort LILRA4+ IL3RA+ cells and validate IRF7, GZMB expression by qPCR or intracellular staining; confirm Type I IFN production (IFN-α/β) by ELISA or intracellular cytokine staining upon TLR7/9 stimulation; single-cell RNA-seq to confirm IRF7+ LILRA4+ GZMB+ cells are pDC, not cDC1/cDC2

programme_name: pDC Interferon Response and Plasma Cell Differentiation
functional_description: This signature represents activated pDCs with dual characteristics: robust Type I interferon production (IRF7) combined with plasmacytoid dendritic cell-specific markers (LILRA4, IL3RA) and features of antibody secretion competence (JCHAIN, MZB1). The co-expression of GZMB suggests cytotoxic capacity, while SERPINF1 indicates immunomodulatory activity consistent with pDC terminal differentiation toward antibody-secreting cells.
key_evidence: IRF7: Master regulator of Type I interferon production, canonical pDC transcription factor
LILRA4: pDC-restricted surface receptor essential for pDC identity and function
IL3RA: CD123, pan-pDC marker enabling IL-3 responsiveness and pDC development
JCHAIN: Immunoglobulin joining chain indicating plasma cell differentiation axis
MZB1: Marginal zone B cell/plasma cell marker, suggests pDC-to-plasmablast transition
GZMB: Cytotoxic granzyme indicating activated, mature pDC phenotype
PLD4: pDC-specific nucleotide sensor involved in TLR-mediated responses
SERPINF1: Immunomodulatory serpin supporting anti-inflammatory pDC function
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining pDCs (LILRA4+, IL3RA+, SIGLEC-H+) for IRF7, GZMB, and JCHAIN expression; RNA-seq of sorted pDCs ±TLR7/9 stimulation; confirm absence of TAP1 and XCR1 to exclude cDC1 contamination

functional_description: This signature represents the core MHC-II antigen presentation machinery in cDC2 dendritic cells, characterized by coordinated expression of HLA class II molecules (DR, DQ, DP) and their essential chaperones. The programme is enriched in cells specializing in CD4+ T cell activation through professional antigen presentation, with supporting evidence for iron homeostasis and protein synthesis capacity required for high-level MHC-II expression.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA: α-chain of HLA-DR, fundamental MHC-II heterodimer for cDC2 antigen presentation
HLA-DRB1: β-chain of HLA-DR, the dominant MHC-II molecule on cDC2
HLA-DMA: non-classical MHC-II chaperone regulating peptide loading in endosomal compartments
HLA-DQA1: α-chain of HLA-DQ, alternative MHC-II presentation pathway
HLA-DQB1: β-chain of HLA-DQ, cooperates with DQA in antigen presentation
HLA-DPA1: α-chain of HLA-DP, third MHC-II molecule expressed on cDC2
HLA-DPB1: β-chain of HLA-DP, completes DP heterodimer for broader peptide presentation
CD74: invariant chain chaperone essential for MHC-II assembly and trafficking
FTH1: ferritin heavy chain supporting iron storage for high metabolic demand of professional APCs
MARCKSL1: cytoskeletal regulator supporting PKC signalling in antigen presentation
RPS2: ribosomal protein supporting elevated protein synthesis in cDC2
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, HLA-DP surface expression with cDC2 markers (CLEC12A+, CD1c+, CD14-low); assess CD4+ T cell activation capacity in vitro using this cDC2 subset; confirm elevated MHC-II compartment organization via confocal microscopy of HLA-DMA/CD74 colocalization

functional_description: This signature reflects a monocytic/pre-DC intermediate state within the cDC2 population, characterized by elevated expression of myeloid differentiation and innate pattern recognition coupled with lysosomal proteolysis. The dominance of S100A8/A9 calprotectin, FCN1 ficolin, and TYROBP-ITAM signalling indicates active TLR/CLR sensing and microbial antigen processing, while elevated CD14 and CTSS suggest cross-differentiation potential or developmental stage-specific activation rather than mature cDC2 cytokine programming.
key_evidence: S100A9: Calcium-binding alarmin; hallmark of monocytic/activated myeloid differentiation; associated with TLR4 signalling amplification
CLEC7A: Dectin-1 (β-glucan receptor); C-type lectin pattern recognition receptor essential for fungal antigen sensing
FCN1: Ficolin-1; collectin family member mediating complement activation and PAMP recognition in innate immunity
TYROBP: DAP12; ITAM-containing adaptor protein coupling CLRs and TLRs to downstream signalling (CARD9, Syk pathway)
CTSS: Cathepsin S; lysosomal protease critical for antigen processing and MHC-II loading (elevated in tissue-resident APCs)
S100A8: Calprotectin subunit; calcium-binding protein and damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) mediating myeloid activation
CD14: LPS co-receptor; monocyte/macrophage marker; elevated expression suggests developmental intermediate or inflammatory state
VCAN: Versican; ECM proteoglycan; associated with inflammatory tissue remodelling and myeloid recruitment
SERPINA1: Alpha-1 antitrypsin; anti-inflammatory protease inhibitor; balances neutrophil elastase in inflamed microenvironments
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining for CD14 intensity, TYROBP, S100A8/A9, and CLEC7A to stratify cDC2 maturation subsets; RNA-seq of sorted CD14-high vs. CD14-low cDC2 populations to confirm monocytic intermediate vs. mature cDC2 transcriptional states; TLR4/CLR activation assays (e.g., TNF-α secretion upon LPS or fungal challenge) to validate functional innate sensing capacity.

functional_description: This signature reflects a subset of mature pDCs with enhanced antibody production and plasma cell-like secretory features, characterized by JCHAIN expression (IgA/immunoglobulin secretion) and SERPINF1 (secreted protease inhibitor). The programme combines pDC maturation markers (PTPRS) with ER/secretory pathway components (DERL3, ITM2C) and minor cytotoxic potential (GZMB), indicating a differentiated pDC state optimized for immunoglobulin-mediated immunity rather than pure Type I IFN production.
key_evidence: JCHAIN: pDC-specific immunoglobulin J chain - hallmark of antibody-secreting plasma cell differentiation
SERPINF1: secreted serpin indicating enhanced protein synthesis and secretory pathway activation
PTPRS: established pDC maturation and migration marker (CCR7/MHC trafficking regulator)
DERL3: ER-resident derlin involved in protein quality control during high-rate secretion
GZMB: minor cytotoxic priming suggesting activated/mature pDC state
ITM2C: ER/Golgi component supporting sustained secretory function
PPP1R14B: innate immune signalling regulator consistent with activated pDC state
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain JCHAIN+ cells with SIGLEC-H+/BST2+/CD123+ and plasmablast markers (CD138, PRDM1); quantify IgA-specific secretion by ELISPOT; assess IRF7/SPIB co-expression to confirm pDC identity versus true plasma cells. RNA-seq on sorted JCHAIN+ pDC subsets to confirm reduced Type I IFN (IRF7, MX1, OAS genes) and enhanced immunoglobulin production compared to canonical pDC.

programme_name: pDC Type I IFN maturation and effector
functional_description: This signature defines mature plasmacytoid dendritic cells committed to type I interferon production and plasma cell-like secretory functions. The dominance of IRF7 and TCF4 (master pDC transcription factors) combined with LILRA4 (canonical pDC marker) and JCHAIN/MZB1 (antibody production machinery) indicates pDCs undergoing terminal maturation with immunoglobulin-secreting cell characteristics, likely in response to nucleic acid stimulation.
key_evidence: IRF7: Master transcription factor for type I IFN production, rate-limiting in pDC antiviral responses
TCF4: Essential pDC identity transcription factor (E2-2), required for pDC lineage specification and TLR7/9 signaling
LILRA4: Canonical pDC-restricted surface marker, present in 91% activating cells
JCHAIN: Immunoglobulin J-chain indicating plasma cell-like secretory differentiation of pDCs
MZB1: Positive regulator of cell proliferation and plasma cell marker, supports antibody secretion phenotype
GZMB: Cytotoxic granule protease supporting pDC effector functions beyond IFN production
SERPINF1: Secreted protease inhibitor consistent with activated pDC inflammatory program
TSPAN13: pDC-enriched tetraspanin involved in surface receptor organization and TLR signaling
BCL11A: Transcription factor regulating immune cell differentiation and pDC development
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation: co-stain pDCs (SIGLEC-H+/BST2+/LILRA4+) for IRF7 and TCF4 phosphorylation/localization; assess JCHAIN/MZB1 co-expression; measure intracellular IFN-β production; compare Type I IFN secretion rates versus cDC1/cDC2 controls

functional_description: This signature represents mature, activated pDCs with concurrent acquisition of cytotoxic effector functions. The co-expression of master pDC transcription factors (IRF7, TCF4) with granzyme B and immunoglobulin-associated genes suggests pDCs undergoing terminal differentiation towards plasmablast-like or cytotoxic-competent states, potentially in response to viral stimulation.
key_evidence: IRF7: Master pDC transcription factor and Type I IFN regulator, essential for pDC identity
TCF4: E2-2 transcription factor required for pDC lineage commitment and development
LILRA4: pDC-specific inhibitory receptor, almost exclusively expressed on pDCs
CLEC4C: BDCA-2, canonical pDC surface marker and TLR7/9 signalling modulator
GZMB: Granzyme B indicates cytotoxic differentiation unusual in steady-state pDCs but consistent with activated/mature states
JCHAIN: J-chain production suggests differentiation toward plasma cell-like phenotype
MZB1: Associated with immunoglobulin secretion and B-cell differentiation, indicating transdifferentiation signature
SERPINF1: Pigment epithelium-derived factor, linked to immunoregulation and pDC function
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: confirm LILRA4+CLEC4C+IRF7+ cells co-express GZMB and assess CD138/CD27 plasma cell markers; bulk RNA-seq of sorted mature vs. resting pDCs; quantify Type I IFN production capability to confirm pDC function is retained despite cytotoxic differentiation markers

programme_name: Proliferative metabolic priming in DC progenitors
functional_description: This signature reflects active cell cycle progression and mitochondrial metabolic engagement in proliferating DC progenitors, predominantly Pre-cDC and Pre-pDC Cycling populations. The coordinated upregulation of mitochondrial respiration genes (MT-CO2, MT-CO3), microtubule dynamics (STMN1, TUBA1B), chromatin remodeling factors (HMGB1, HMGB2, H2AFZ), and cell cycle checkpoint regulators (PCLAF, NUCKS1) indicates S/G2-M phase progenitors undergoing clonal expansion with enhanced oxidative metabolism.
key_evidence: STMN1: Canonical cell cycle regulator; microtubule organizing protein essential for mitotic progression
MT-CO2, MT-CO3: Mitochondrial electron transport chain components indicating heightened oxidative phosphorylation in cycling progenitors
PCLAF: S-phase specific centrosome and chromatin factor; direct marker of cell cycle progression
HMGB1, HMGB2: Chromatin architectural proteins facilitating transcriptional remodeling during progenitor expansion
NUCKS1: Casein kinase II substrate with phosphorylation sites; involved in cell cycle checkpoint control
TUBA1B: Tubulin required for mitotic spindle assembly; indicator of M-phase commitment
H2AFZ, HMGN2: Histone variants and chromatin modifiers supporting active transcription in cycling cells
ANP32B: Apoptosis regulator preventing programmed cell death in expanding progenitor pools
suggested_validation: Validate via flow cytometry co-staining Pre-cDC/Pre-pDC with Ki-67, PCNA, and mitochondrial potential dyes (TMRM/JC-1); perform single-cell metabolic profiling (Seahorse/Oroboros) to confirm oxidative capacity in sorted cycling progenitors; correlate FLT3L stimulation-induced proliferation with signature activation kinetics.

functional_description: This signature reflects a metabolically active, proliferating Pre-cDC population characterized by elevated expression of core histones (H2AFZ, H3F3A), high-mobility group proteins (HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN2), and cytoskeletal components (TUBA1B, TUBB, STMN1). The programme integrates cell cycle progression with chromatin dynamics and nucleoprotein remodelling, consistent with active proliferation and transcriptional plasticity in committed cDC progenitors.
key_evidence: STMN1: Mitotic regulator and cell cycle checkpoint protein, enriched in cycling Pre-cDC
H2AFZ: Histone variant essential for nucleosome stability and transcriptional regulation during proliferation
HMGB1/HMGB2: Chromatin remodellers supporting transcriptional activity and DNA damage response in dividing cells
TUBA1B/TUBB: Structural microtubule components required for mitotic spindle assembly and cytokinesis
HMGN2: Marks transcriptionally active chromatin, associated with open chromatin in proliferating cells
PCLAF: PCNA-associated factor involved in centrosome cycle and DNA replication licensing
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic regulator sustaining survival during intensive proliferation
PPIA: Prolyl isomerase facilitating protein folding during rapid biosynthesis
suggested_validation: Sort Pre-cDC by STMN1/HMGB1/H2AFZ co-expression and validate S/G2-M enrichment via Ki-67 immunostaining or FACS; confirm CLEC12A+PTPRS+ phenotype; assess mitotic index and BrdU incorporation in STMN1-high vs STMN1-low Pre-cDC subsets.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated oxidative phosphorylation and protein synthesis capacity in Pre-cDC progenitors, characterized by upregulation of mitochondrial electron transport chain components (MT-CO3, MT-CO2, MT-ND1, UQCRH) and ribosomal proteins. The enrichment suggests Pre-cDC are metabolically active cells with high ATP demand to support rapid proliferation and differentiation toward committed cDC lineages.
key_evidence: MT-CO3, MT-CO2, MT-ND1, UQCRH: Core mitochondrial respiratory chain complex I and IV components indicating elevated OXPHOS in metabolically active Pre-cDC
RPS26, RPS24, RPS17: Ribosomal 40S subunit proteins indicating enhanced translational capacity for biosynthesis during progenitor expansion
AIF1: Cytokine-responsive calcium-binding protein associated with myeloid cell activation and cytokine signaling in developing DC progenitors
S100A4, TMSB4X: Actin-regulating and cell migration proteins consistent with Pre-cDC mobilization and developmental plasticity
GSTP1, BLVRB: Antioxidant and heme metabolism enzymes protecting against oxidative stress from elevated mitochondrial activity
Cell composition 63.5% Pre-cDC: Strong enrichment validates Pre-cDC progenitor identity over mature cDC1/cDC2
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry quantification of mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM/JC-1) and protein synthesis rate (pS6K) in CLEC12A+PTPRS+ Pre-cDC versus mature cDC subsets; RT-qPCR validation of MT-CO genes and RPS transcripts; functional assessment via 13C-glucose tracing to confirm OXPHOS dependency in Pre-cDC expansion

programme_name: pDC type I interferon production and maturation
functional_description: This signature reflects mature, activated plasmacytoid dendritic cells with prominent type I interferon response capability. The co-expression of IRF7 (master regulator of type I IFN production in pDC) with LILRA4 and IL3RA (canonical pDC surface markers) and JCHAIN (immunoglobulin J-chain, indicating plasma cell-like antibody secretion capacity) defines a functionally distinct pDC subset. The presence of GZMB suggests cytotoxic capacity typical of activated pDC in antiviral responses.
key_evidence: IRF7: master transcription factor for type I interferon production in pDC; ranks 3rd in Welch t-statistic
LILRA4: canonical pDC-specific immunomodulatory surface receptor; definitive pDC lineage marker
IL3RA: CD123, the alpha chain of IL-3 receptor; pDC-specific surface marker absent in cDC1/cDC2
JCHAIN: J-chain for immunoglobulin assembly; indicates pDC capacity for antibody secretion and plasma cell differentiation
GZMB: granzyme B for cytotoxic granule-mediated killing; activated pDC cytotoxic function
Cell composition: 69.5% pDC dominance confirms pDC-enriched signature despite ANOVA rank 130
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation: sort pDC (SIGLEC-H+ BST2+ LILRA4+) vs cDC2 (CD11c+ CLEC4A+ CCR7+) and perform qPCR for IRF7, MX1, OAS1, GZMB, and JCHAIN expression; single-cell RNA-seq within LILRA4+ IL3RA+ subset; assess type I IFN secretion by intracellular cytokine staining (IFN-β/α) following TLR9 stimulation

functional_description: This signature reflects a monocyte-like inflammatory cDC2 subset with enhanced lysosomal proteolysis, pattern recognition receptor signalling, and innate immune activation. The programme is characterised by S100 alarm signals, complement activation, and cysteine protease-mediated antigen processing, suggesting cDC2 cells poised for rapid inflammatory responses rather than steady-state antigen presentation.
key_evidence: CLEC7A: Dectin-1 pattern recognition receptor drives inflammatory cDC2 responses
S100A9/S100A8: Alarmin-mediated calcium signalling and myeloid differentiation markers
CTSS: Cathepsin S essential for MHC-II peptide generation in DC
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor coupling pattern recognition to inflammatory signalling
FCN1: Ficolin innate pattern recognition and complement activation pathway
VCAN: Extracellular matrix interactions supporting inflammatory microenvironment
CD14: Co-receptor for TLR4 signalling in monocyte-like cDC2
CFD: Complement alternative pathway activation amplifying inflammation
PSAP: Lysosomal saposin processing for lipid antigen presentation
LGALS2: Lectin-mediated immune regulation and lymphotoxin interactions
suggested_validation: Sort cDC2 by CLEC7A/CD14/S100A9 co-expression and validate lysosomal protease activity (CTSS/LGALS2) via flow cytometry. Confirm TYROBP-dependent signalling using phorbol ester stimulation and phospho-p65 readouts. Measure complement activation (CFD) and inflammatory cytokine production (TNF/IL-12) to distinguish this inflammatory cDC2 subset from steady-state CD1c+ cDC2.

functional_description: This signature represents the core MHC class II antigen presentation machinery in cDC2 cells, with dominant expression of HLA-DR, HLA-DP, and HLA-DQ heterodimeric components. The coordinated upregulation of HLA-DRA, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DMA and their corresponding beta chains reflects the mature antigen-presenting capacity characteristic of professional cDC2s, supported by iron homeostasis (FTH1) required for metabolic demand.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA: alpha chain of HLA-DR, canonical cDC2 MHC-II molecule
HLA-DRB1: beta chain of HLA-DR, essential for cDC2 peptide presentation
HLA-DPA1: alpha chain of HLA-DP, cDC2-enriched MHC-II pathway
HLA-DPB1: beta chain of HLA-DP, cDC2-specific antigen presentation
HLA-DQB1: beta chain of HLA-DQ, complete MHC-II repertoire
HLA-DMA: peptide loading catalyst for MHC-II in endosomal compartments
FTH1: iron storage protein supporting high metabolic/translational demand of cDC2
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor for Fc receptor integration in cDC2 activation
S100A6: calcium-binding protein involved in cDC2 differentiation signals
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry confirming HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ surface protein co-expression on CLEC12A+CD1c+ cDC2s; functional assay of allogeneic T cell activation with cDC2s versus cDC1 controls; RNA-seq of sorted CLEC12A+ cDC2s versus XCR1+ cDC1s to confirm MHC-II enrichment

functional_description: This signature reflects a transitional or activated state shared between pDC (69%) and cDC2 (30%) characterized by cytotoxic granule proteins, endoplasmic reticulum stress responses, and IRF4-mediated transcriptional control. The enrichment of GZMB and cytotoxic machinery suggests activated pDC with enhanced effector functions rather than canonical Type I IFN-dominated pDC, while PTPRS implicates pDC maturation signaling.
key_evidence: GZMB: cytotoxic granule serine protease marking activated, cytotoxic pDC and cDC2 populations
IRF4: master TF for DC maturation and effector differentiation; supports cDC2 and activated pDC
PTPRS: pDC-specific maturation and migration marker; confirmed in expert panel
JCHAIN: antibody-linked immunity suggesting plasma cell-like differentiation in activated pDC subset
SERPINF1: tissue remodeling and anti-apoptotic factor consistent with activated DC phenotype
DERL3 + CLIC3: ER-resident protein quality control and chloride transport; stress response signatures
SMPD3 + PPP1R14B: exosomal signaling and innate immune phosphatase regulation in activated state
suggested_validation: Sort pDC and cDC2 by GZMB/SERPINF1 high vs. low expression; validate IRF4 nuclear localization and phospho-STAT signaling in activated pDC subset; confirm absence of cross-presentation markers (TAP1, XCR1) to rule out cDC1 contamination; measure Type I IFN secretion (IFN-α/β) in GZMB+ vs. GZMB- pDC to assess if this represents true pDC or mis-sorted cDC2.

functional_description: This signature reflects constitutive housekeeping and nucleoprotein functions enriched in Pre-cDC progenitors, characterized by ribosomal proteins, glycolytic enzymes, and chromatin-associated factors. The dominance of translational machinery (RPS2, RPS24, RPS23) and metabolic housekeeping (GAPDH, PPIA) suggests high biosynthetic activity typical of committed cDC progenitors. Chromatin remodeling factors (HMGN1, HMGB1, H2AFY, YBX1) indicate active transcriptional regulation without lineage-specific commitment signals.
key_evidence: PTMA: DNA-binding factor activity and apoptotic regulation in actively developing progenitors
GAPDH: Glycolytic moonlighting protein indicating elevated metabolic state of Pre-cDC
HMGN1: Nucleosomal DNA binding associated with transcriptionally active chromatin in progenitors
RPS2/RPS24/RPS23: Ribosomal proteins reflecting high protein synthesis demands of differentiating progenitors
HMGB1: Non-histone nuclear protein regulating transcription and DNA organization in committed precursors
YBX1: RNA/DNA-binding protein with broad regulatory roles in progenitor differentiation
MT-CO2/MT-CO3: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation supporting energy demands of Pre-cDC expansion
suggested_validation: Validate Pre-cDC identity by flow cytometry co-staining CLEC12A+PTPRS+ with surface markers CCR7-low, and confirm lack of IRF8/IRF4/SPIB lineage commitment by RNA-FISH. Compare signature activation across FACS-sorted Pre-cDC vs mature cDC1/cDC2 to confirm progenitor-enrichment pattern.

programme_name: pDC identity and type I IFN readiness
functional_description: This signature defines mature plasmacytoid dendritic cells with established identity markers and poised type I interferon production capacity. The co-expression of master transcription factors (IRF7, TCF4, SPIB), pDC-restricted surface receptors (LILRA4, IL3RA), and cytoplasmic B-cell-associated factors (JCHAIN, MZB1) indicates differentiated pDCs with functional capacity for both innate immune sensing and IFN response.
key_evidence: IRF7: Master regulator of type I IFN production and pDC maturation; critical for TLR7/9 signaling
TCF4: Essential E2-2 transcription factor for pDC lineage specification and identity maintenance
SPIB: Lymphoid-restricted PU-box transcription factor critical for pDC development
LILRA4: Canonical pDC surface marker; inhibitory receptor on pDCs modulating immune responses
IL3RA: CD123, pDC-selective cytokine receptor; highest expression in pDC subset
JCHAIN: Immunoglobulin joining chain; marker of plasmacytoid morphology and antibody secretion capacity
MZB1: B-cell maturation factor; indicates pDC subset with secretory differentiation potential
PLD4: Nuclease involved in viral nucleic acid sensing; supports pDC antiviral function
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining (LILRA4+/IL3RA+/SIGLEC-H+) combined with qPCR validation of IRF7, TCF4, SPIB expression. Functional validation via TLR7/9 stimulation assays to confirm Type I IFN production capacity in this subset.

programme_name: pDC cytotoxic maturation and interferon response
functional_description: This signature reflects a subset of pDCs with enhanced cytotoxic effector capacity and Type I interferon regulatory machinery, characterized by granzyme B expression alongside the master pDC transcription factor IRF7. The co-expression of pDC-specific markers (LILRA4) with cytotoxic granule proteins (GZMB) and immunoglobulin J-chain (JCHAIN) suggests activated, antibody-secreting pDCs capable of both interferon production and direct cytotoxic function.
key_evidence: IRF7: Master transcription factor for Type I IFN production in pDCs; ranks 5th in Welch t-statistic
LILRA4: pDC-specific surface marker (CD85g); validates pDC identity of activating cell population
GZMB: Cytotoxic granule protein indicating pDC activation and effector differentiation state
JCHAIN: J-chain component of dimeric IgA, suggesting differentiation toward antibody-secreting plasma cell-like pDCs
SERPINF1: Serpin family protease inhibitor; supports cytotoxic/inflammatory pDC phenotype
Cell composition: 56.5% pDC dominance confirms pDC-centric signature despite cDC2 contribution
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining: LILRA4+ cells for IRF7 nuclear expression, GZMB content, and surface immunoglobulin markers; RNA-seq of sorted LILRA4+GZMB+ versus LILRA4+GZMB- pDCs to confirm IRF7-dependent cytotoxic effector program; functional assay measuring Type I IFN secretion and cytotoxic activity in GZMB+ pDC subset

functional_description: This signature reflects pre-cDC developmental commitment with strong MHC class II antigen presentation machinery (HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1, CD74, HLA-DMA). The dominance of Pre-cDC cells (61.5%) and co-expression of housekeeping genes with cysteine protease inhibition (CST3) suggests a maturing cDC2-committed progenitor population acquiring antigen-presenting capacity. The signature lacks cDC1/pDC lineage markers (IRF8, SPIB, SIGLEC-H) and cycling markers, indicating post-proliferative, lineage-restricted development.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA: canonical MHC-II alpha chain, marks antigen-presenting cells and cDC2 trajectory
HLA-DRB1: MHC-II beta chain essential for peptide-MHC complex formation, cDC2-biased expression
CD74: MHC-II-associated invariant chain chaperone, antigen processing determinant
HLA-DMA: MHC-II peptide-loading facilitator, maturation-associated upregulation
CST3: cysteine protease inhibitor supporting intracellular proteolysis control during DC maturation
COTL1: actin-binding protein, cytoskeletal remodelling in differentiating progenitors
Pre-cDC dominance (61.5%): confirms cDC2 lineage commitment signature
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain Pre-cDC marker (CLEC12A+) with HLA-DR, CD74 surface expression; FACS sorting followed by qPCR validation of IRF4 vs IRF8 expression ratio to confirm cDC2 vs cDC1 bias; single-cell RNA-seq trajectory analysis from ASDC→Pre-cDC→cDC2 developmental continuum

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein and translation factor expression characteristic of actively biosynthetically engaged DC progenitors, particularly Pre-pDC and Pre-cDC populations. The enrichment of ribosomal subunit components (RPS2, RPS24, RPL4, RPL7A, RPLP0) and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) indicates heightened translational capacity required for rapid protein production during progenitor expansion. Concurrent expression of cell cycle regulators (NPM1, H3F3A histone variant) and cytoskeletal proteins (ACTG1) supports active cell division and morphodynamic remodeling in uncommitted progenitor cells.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPS24, RPL4, RPL7A, RPLP0: Ribosomal protein structural components indicating elevated global translation capacity
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor required for efficient protein synthesis during rapid progenitor expansion
NPM1: Cell cycle and centrosome regulator; marks proliferative progenitor populations
H3F3A, H2AFY: Histone variants associated with active chromatin remodeling in cycling cells
ACTG1: Cytoskeletal actin required for cell division and morphological plasticity
SLC25A3: Mitochondrial phosphate transporter supporting energy metabolism in biosynthetically active cells
suggested_validation: Validate via flow cytometry measuring Ki-67 co-expression with CD135+ (FLT3+) DC progenitors; confirm elevated protein synthesis rates using puromycin incorporation assays; perform ribosome profiling to assess translation efficiency bias toward lineage-determination genes (SPIB, IRF4, IRF8) in Pre-pDC vs Pre-cDC subsets

functional_description: This signature reflects a differentiated pDC state characterized by dual activation of Type I interferon regulatory circuits (IRF7, TCF4) and antibody-secreting cell (ASC) programming. The co-expression of JCHAIN, MZB1, and SERPINF1 indicates pDC engagement in plasmacell differentiation or cooperation with B cells, while LILRA4 and IL3RA confirm pDC identity.
key_evidence: TCF4: Master transcription factor for pDC specification and Type I IFN production
IRF7: Central pDC Type I interferon regulator; elevated in activated pDC
LILRA4: pDC-specific surface marker; absent from cDC1/cDC2
IL3RA: CD123; canonical pDC marker (IL-3 responsiveness)
JCHAIN: Immunoglobulin J chain; indicates ASC differentiation or pDC-B cell cooperation
MZB1: Marginal zone B cell/ASC-associated; suggests pDC role in antibody responses
GZMB: Cytotoxic effector; pDC express upon activation for infected cell elimination
SERPINF1: Immunomodulatory serpin; supports anti-inflammatory pDC phenotype
PPP1R14B: Innate immune signaling; consistent with active TLR7/9 sensing
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of LILRA4/IL3RA/TCF4/IRF7 on pDC subsets; quantify Type I IFN (IFN-α/β) production by intracellular cytokine staining; validate JCHAIN/MZB1 upregulation in pDC co-cultured with activated B cells to confirm ASC programming axis.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated translational machinery and oxidative phosphorylation capacity in DC progenitors, particularly Pre-cDC and Pre-pDC populations. The enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPS17, RPS24, RPS26, RPL37A, RPLP0) and mitochondrial respiratory chain components (MT-CO2, MT-ND1, UQCRH, ATP5J2, ATP5G3) indicates heightened biosynthetic and metabolic activity characteristic of proliferating or metabolically active progenitor cells preparing for differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS17/RPS24/RPS26/RPL37A/RPLP0: 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit proteins driving protein synthesis capacity in Pre-cDC (35%) and Pre-pDC (23.5%) populations
MT-CO2/MT-ND1/UQCRH: Mitochondrial electron transport chain components enabling ATP production for energy-demanding progenitor differentiation
ATP5J2/ATP5G3: ATP synthase subunits coupling oxidative phosphorylation to support metabolic demand
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor facilitating ribosome function during active protein synthesis
MIF: Immunoregulatory cytokine priming immune-competent differentiation in developing progenitors
Pre-cDC/Pre-pDC enrichment: 58.5% of activating cells are committed DC progenitors with high translational/metabolic capacity
suggested_validation: Validate metabolic activation via seahorse mitochondrial stress assays and protein synthesis rates (puromycin incorporation) comparing Pre-cDC, Pre-pDC, and mature cDC1/cDC2/pDC. Confirm ribosomal biogenesis through nucleolar markers (NPM1, FBL) and assess whether this signature predicts progenitor fitness and differentiation competency.

programme_name: pDC Type I Interferon Production Program
functional_description: This signature reflects mature, Type I interferon-producing pDC with active transcriptional control via TCF4 (E2-2) and IRF7, combined with evidence of cytotoxic granule production (GZMB) and secretory machinery activation. The strong pDC enrichment (90%) and presence of master regulators TCF4/IRF7 indicate committed pDC identity with functional Type I IFN capacity.
key_evidence: TCF4: Master transcription factor (E2-2) essential for pDC lineage specification and Type I IFN production
IRF7: Critical regulator of Type I interferon response; defines pDC's high per-cell IFN secretion capacity
LILRA4: pDC-specific surface marker; cell-intrinsic immune checkpoint regulating TLR-induced responses
GZMB: Indicates cytotoxic pDC subset capable of granzyme B-mediated killing alongside IFN production
PLD4: Nucleotide sensor localisation in endosomal compartments; supports TLR7/9 nucleic acid sensing
MZB1: pDC-enriched secretory pathway protein; supports Type I IFN protein synthesis and export
JCHAIN: Immunoglobulin-associated; indicates IgA-producing, antibody-secreting differentiation state
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation: pDC (SIGLEC-H+LILRA4+) sorting followed by intracellular IFN-β/TNF-α staining; qPCR quantification of IRF7 and MX1/IFIT1 target genes; functional assay: TLR7/9 agonist stimulation measuring Type I IFN secretion in TCF4+ vs TCF4− populations

programme_name: Metabolic and lysosomal maturation in cDC2
functional_description: This signature reflects enhanced oxidative phosphorylation and proteasomal/lysosomal proteolytic capacity in cDC2 cells, consistent with metabolic support for antigen processing and presentation. The enrichment of ATP synthase subunits (ATP5J2, ATP5F1, ATP5C1, ATP5A1, ATP5B) alongside CTSS (cathepsin S) indicates active energy metabolism coupled with lysosomal cysteine protease activity required for MHC-II peptide generation. Co-expression of GRN and S100A11 suggests inflammatory priming and calcium signaling associated with DC activation.
key_evidence: ATP5J2, ATP5F1, ATP5C1, ATP5A1, ATP5B: Oxidative phosphorylation complex V subunits indicating elevated energy production for biosynthetic demands of antigen-presenting cells
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease essential for processing exogenous antigens into peptides for MHC-II presentation in professional APCs
GRN: Secreted granulins with immunomodulatory functions supporting inflammatory responses and cell activation in mature dendritic cells
TMSB4X: Actin-binding protein regulating cytoskeletal dynamics required for migration and antigen presentation efficiency
PSMA2, ATPIF1: Proteasomal components supporting endogenous antigen processing and MHC-I cross-presentation
S100A11: Calcium-binding protein implicated in DC activation and inflammatory signaling
suggested_validation: Validate with flow cytometry measuring ATP synthase expression (OXPHOS), CTSS activity assays, and co-staining with cDC2 markers (CLEC12A, CD1c). Correlate with functional assays of antigen presentation capacity and cytokine production (IL12B, TNF). Cross-reference with proteomic data on mitochondrial and lysosomal compartments in mature cDC2 versus precursors.

functional_description: This signature represents terminally differentiated pDC with concurrent plasmacytoid features, characterized by immunoglobulin secretion machinery (JCHAIN, MZB1) and type I IFN regulatory capacity (IRF7). The co-expression of cytotoxic effectors (GZMB) alongside plasma cell markers suggests activated pDC with antibody-secreting potential, distinct from canonical pDC interferon production.
key_evidence: LILRA4: Canonical pDC surface marker (78.5% pDC composition)
IRF7: Master regulator of type I interferon response in pDC
JCHAIN: J-chain for immunoglobulin polymerization, indicating plasma cell differentiation
MZB1: Positive regulator of B/plasma cell proliferation and Ig secretion
GZMB: Cytotoxic effector molecule, atypical but present in activated pDC
PLD4: Nucleotide-sensing pathway component relevant to pDC TLR signalling
SERPINF1: Secreted immunomodulatory protein consistent with activated pDC phenotype
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation: co-stain LILRA4+ cells for JCHAIN/MZB1/IRF7 expression; quantify intracellular IgA/IgM; perform single-cell RNA-seq with protein to confirm plasma cell transcription factors (XBP1, PRDM1) co-expression with pDC markers; assess functional capacity for both IFN-α production and antibody secretion.
